title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
content_c:
Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
- Published
Ukraine has stabilised the front line and "broken Russia's ability to advance" by killing so many of its men, Ukraine's former commander-in-chief has claimed in an interview with the BBC.
Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi made the comments in an exclusive interview, his first since he was dramatically forced from his post in the summer.
He addressed his sacking, disagreeing with his critics who declared him too "old school" to command Ukraine's new, technologically advanced forces.
He also pushed back against allegations made by soldiers who previously served under him, who told the BBC they were ordered to remain at their positions even when they were almost surrounded by Russians, leading to high losses.
Syrskyi said that Moscow's overall losses in the war were six times higher than Ukraine's. "If you count only dead, then it's up to 11 times," he added.
Neither Russia nor Ukraine officially release the numbers of their dead. Ukraine's military says it inflicted record losses this year on Russian soldiers in September, although that cannot be verified.
UK intelligence chiefs estimate Russia has lost around half a million men killed in Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022. The US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies meanwhile believes, external Ukraine has lost up to 150,000 troops killed by June 2026.
He says this difference in death toll – as well as technological advances, and a strategy of attacking weak points in Russia's lines while containing their advances in other parts – accounts for the current stalemate at the front.
In the first six months of 2026, Russia managed overall to seize 61 sq km, the general said. "It's an indication that the front line has been stabilised."
The Institute for Study of War (ISW) has also confirmed this trend. One of its recent reports, external says that in September 2026, Moscow lost more territory than it took.
Syrskyi was appointed Ukraine's commander-in-chief in 2024. He had previously won praise for defending Kyiv at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, and for leading the successful counteroffensive east of Kharkiv in the autumn of that year.
But President Volodymyr Zelensky fired Syrskyi this summer, amid a major disagreement with then-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
Fedorov had said that instead of adapting to the realities of the changing war, the army under Syrskyi had blocked his initiatives.
Zelensky initially fired Fedorov, as tensions burst into the open between the two men. But mass street protests then forced the president to also fire Syrskyi, replacing him with Maj Gen Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43.
Syrskyi told the BBC that he had "disagreements" with Fedorov because the latter "didn't take into consideration the interests of the army" when procuring weapons and supplies.
Fedorov had created an "imbalance" in supplies, Syrskyi said. He had prioritised drones while overlooking key front-line kit such as unmanned ground vehicles, pick-up trucks and motorbikes. Even with drones, Syrskyi said, there were shortages as the army got only half of what they needed.
Fedorov was a popular young minister who was known for his digital and technological initiatives. Many contrasted him with Syrskyi, who critics thought was not fit to lead the new technological arms race with Russia.
But Syrskyi disagrees with such criticism. It was during his time the use of drones reached this new, unprecedented level, including deep strikes more than 2,000km (1,200 miles) behind enemy lines, he said. Ukraine was the first country to create the Unmanned Systems Forces as a separate branch of armed forces, under his command: now, he said, drones account for 80% of Russia's losses.
Under his military leadership, however, Ukrainian troops undertook chaotic withdrawals from the eastern cities of Avdiivka and Vuhledar, and from around Pokrovsk.
Soldiers who spoke to the BBC in the past complained that they were ordered to remain at their positions at any costs. By the time they were told to pull back, it was often too late as they were almost surrounded by Russian troops.
Syrskyi does not deny that such situations occur on the front line. But he told the BBC that Ukraine was fighting against a far more powerful army.
In 2025, the ratio of jets and bombs was 18 to one in Moscow's favour, he said. In the same year, Russia had two-and-a-half times more artillery pieces and shells than Ukraine. And with four million militarily trained men who they can mobilise, Russian forces can create chances to push through, he argued.
One of Syrskyi's most famous operations was an incursion into Russia's Kursk region that started in August 2024. It ended with a dramatic retreat the following spring, which some soldiers described as "catastrophic". Syrskyi, however, insisted that the Kursk operation was "a necessity".
"In the summer 2024, Russian forces were pushing along all main directions on the front line with up to six times more troops than we had," he explained.
The Kursk incursion disrupted Russia's offensive and forced Moscow to redirect troops, giving Ukraine a respite and a chance for its stretched brigades in the east and south to recover, Syrskyi said.
He also had strong words for European allies who doubt that Russia may have territorial ambitions beyond Ukraine. He advised European partners to start preparing for the war now and "drop all illusions that [it] will not come".
He also said he believed Ukraine's war was going to become even more technological. There will be more robots, automated systems and artificial intelligence (AI). "Even ordinary weapons now get an AI-based control system to enhance their capabilities," he said.
Such technologies can give a new life to conventional weapons like tanks. Both Russia and Ukraine were now racing to develop "active systems of defence" to protect armoured vehicles, Syrskyi said.
But he insisted that "the human role will remain definitive [on the battlefield] because [people] will need to control those systems".

  - Published1 day ago

title: Burnham to push for new post-Brexit deals at EU summit
content_c:
Burnham to push for new post-Brexit deals at EU summit
- Published
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told MPs he will push for new post-Brexit deals with the EU at a summit next month.
He said "deeper cooperation" on some key issues - including youth mobility, food and drink, and energy - would help drive economic growth in the UK.
In a statement to MPs, Burnham also warned the EU's Made In Europe plans posed "a risk to UK manufacturing" and said he was in talks to get "an arrangement" that worked for the UK. The EU proposals aim to protect EU industry from Chinese competitors but could impact British industry and supply chains.
But Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the prime minister was "unpicking" the deal the UK signed with the EU.
Although he said he was keen to negotiate a closer relationship with the EU, Burnham made clear Labour's manifesto commitments not to return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement, would stay in place until the next election.
Burnham said the "immediate priority" was securing a successful outcome at the November summit, adding: "I believe we should then set up a serious dialogue about the different options for our relationship in the long term.
"At every stage, the British public will be the boss, and I am clear that public opinion currently supports a pragmatic approach like the one I am suggesting."
While the prime minister has committed to the current Labour manifesto's red lines about Brexit, in interviews after Labour conference, he did not rule out a new manifesto, which could include re-joining the EU.
It is increasingly clear that economic growth, and cooperation on illegal immigration, are going to be at the centre of No 10's arguments when it comes to selling a closer relationship both at - and beyond - next month's summit.
The Brexit withdrawal agreement in 2020 agreed the UK's "divorce bill" payments to the EU, and allowed the rules and regulations in the UK to start to diverge from those in the EU, which was necessary in order to negotiate trade deal with other countries.
But the divergence in food standards caused problems for UK food exports to its largest market, a problem that Sir Keir Starmer started to try to fix by renegotiating some common rules to reduce red tape.
In May 2025, this resulted in a post-Brexit deal agreeing continued access to UK waters for EU fishing boats until 2038, in return for a deal to reduce checks on food exports to the EU, which meant the UK was able to sell raw burgers and sausages back into the EU for the first time since Brexit.
The summit next month will see a series of deals with the EU on the table, Burnham told MPs, including food and drink, energy trading, and coordinating on immigration.
Burnham claimed these agreements could add the equivalent of £10bn per year to the economy by 2040, arguing that it would be a "dereliction of duty" to turn away from the chance to cut bureaucracy.
"At present entire truckloads of plants or fresh produce can be destroyed because of a single missing stamp or a minor paperwork delay," he said.
"Fresh meat and fish spoil while waiting in trucks, and tonnes of exports have to be written off. Our largest food export, Scottish salmon, faces a 100% rate of document checks at the border, costing us around £100m in lost exports.
"British burgers and other fresh meat products cannot be sold in the EU, seed potatoes from Scotland and shellfish from Wales are banned - this is having a real impact on businesses and the agreement on the table could reverse some of that damage."
The prime minister said a fresh agreement at the EU summit would also "ease the pressure on prices in the supermarket".
He said securing an energy deal, involving emissions trading, could "lower energy costs for households and businesses alike", adding this could cut wholesale energy costs by 20% in Northern Ireland.
Burnham said he also hoped to rebuild links with EU police and security agencies to boost information-sharing and help tackle smuggling gangs.
And he said being open about a new relationship with the EU was necessary to get a good deal on all these things: "If we are serious about promoting growth, controlling immigration, upholding our values and security, it is a conversation we must have.
"Sticking with the status quo is not good enough for Britain."
- Ten years on, Brexit's economic impact is becoming clearer 
  - Published14 September
- Who are the winners and losers from the UK-EU agreement? 
  - Published19 May 2025
The Conservative leader criticised the prime minister for "unpicking the deal this country signed with the EU a decade after the referendum".
Badenoch added Burnham would not get a better deal than the one secured by the Conservatives, accusing him of giving the game away ahead of the summit.
"His exact words earlier this year were, 'the last thing we should do right now is re-run those arguments' and yet here he is unpicking the deal this country signed with the EU a decade after the referendum," she said.
"He is not going to get a better deal. The EU are tough negotiators, and it's not just that the EU are tough negotiators, he has already revealed his entire negotiating hand.
"He has just blurted out everything he wants in this statement and I will tell him now, as a former trade secretary, this is not how you conduct negotiations."
Mocking the previous negotiations, Burnham said: "She says that, oh, I've revealed what I want to do and this isn't any way to negotiate it - because the Tories were so good, weren't they, at negotiating deals with our partners?"
Conservative Nigel Huddleston pointed out that post-Brexit trade deals with countries like the US and India meant a new EU deal would not be straightforward.
He said: "As a former trade minister can I also advise the PM, because his officials and minsters clearly have not, that actually it may not be as easy after all, because of clauses in some of the 70-something other trade deals that we did with other countries, to unwind all the things he would like to do."
However, Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey welcomed Burnham's recognition of the "damage" of Brexit and called on him to go further, dropping Labour's red lines and opening negotiations on joining the EU single market and customs union.

The summit next month will see a series of deals with the EU on the table, Burnham told MPs, including food and drink, energy trading, and coordinating on immigration.
Burnham claimed these agreements could add the equivalent of £10bn per year to the economy by 2040, arguing that it would be a "dereliction of duty" to turn away from the chance to cut bureaucracy.
"At present entire truckloads of plants or fresh produce can be destroyed because of a single missing stamp or a minor paperwork delay," he said.
"Fresh meat and fish spoil while waiting in trucks, and tonnes of exports have to be written off. Our largest food export, Scottish salmon, faces a 100% rate of document checks at the border, costing us around £100m in lost exports.
"British burgers and other fresh meat products cannot be sold in the EU, seed potatoes from Scotland and shellfish from Wales are banned - this is having a real impact on businesses and the agreement on the table could reverse some of that damage."
The prime minister said a fresh agreement at the EU summit would also "ease the pressure on prices in the supermarket".
He said securing an energy deal, involving emissions trading, could "lower energy costs for households and businesses alike", adding this could cut wholesale energy costs by 20% in Northern Ireland.
Burnham said he also hoped to rebuild links with EU police and security agencies to boost information-sharing and help tackle smuggling gangs.
And he said being open about a new relationship with the EU was necessary to get a good deal on all these things: "If we are serious about promoting growth, controlling immigration, upholding our values and security, it is a conversation we must have.
"Sticking with the status quo is not good enough for Britain."
- Ten years on, Brexit's economic impact is becoming clearer 
  - Published14 September
- Who are the winners and losers from the UK-EU agreement? 
  - Published19 May 2025
The Conservative leader criticised the prime minister for "unpicking the deal this country signed with the EU a decade after the referendum".
Badenoch added Burnham would not get a better deal than the one secured by the Conservatives, accusing him of giving the game away ahead of the summit.
"His exact words earlier this year were, 'the last thing we should do right now is re-run those arguments' and yet here he is unpicking the deal this country signed with the EU a decade after the referendum," she said.
"He is not going to get a better deal. The EU are tough negotiators, and it's not just that the EU are tough negotiators, he has already revealed his entire negotiating hand.
"He has just blurted out everything he wants in this statement and I will tell him now, as a former trade secretary, this is not how you conduct negotiations."
Mocking the previous negotiations, Burnham said: "She says that, oh, I've revealed what I want to do and this isn't any way to negotiate it - because the Tories were so good, weren't they, at negotiating deals with our partners?"
Conservative Nigel Huddleston pointed out that post-Brexit trade deals with countries like the US and India meant a new EU deal would not be straightforward.
He said: "As a former trade minister can I also advise the PM, because his officials and minsters clearly have not, that actually it may not be as easy after all, because of clauses in some of the 70-something other trade deals that we did with other countries, to unwind all the things he would like to do."
However, Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey welcomed Burnham's recognition of the "damage" of Brexit and called on him to go further, dropping Labour's red lines and opening negotiations on joining the EU single market and customs union.

title: UK growth upgraded but energy prices and rates to bite in 2027
content_c:
UK growth upgraded but energy prices and rates to bite in 2027
- Published
The UK economy is forecast to grow by more than previously expected this year before higher energy prices and interest rates hit growth in 2027, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has said.
The organisation's latest report, which is closely watched by the government, said the UK economy would expand by 1.3% in 2026, up from the 1% it predicted in July, before slowing in 2027.
Economies across the world have proved more resilient to the energy price shock caused by the US-Iran war, the IMF said, but it warned the economic fallout from the conflict remained "highly uncertain".
Chancellor John Healey said the government would look to "provide some breathing space" for households in the Budget.
Healey is making the final preparations to Andy Burnham's new-look government's tax and spending plans, which will be announced on 28 October.
Government borrowing costs have surged, placing pressure on the chancellor to ensure his plans are credible in the eyes of financial markets, which the UK relies on to borrow money.
But IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro told BBC News on Tuesday that the UK's process of managing its debts is now leading the major G7 economies.
"As you know, the UK has already started the consolidation process and it is the country that basically stands out, along with India", she said.
The organisation said the UK is one of the only major economies on course to stabilise levels of national debt. It projects the UK will reduce its annual borrowing by nearly four percentage points of GDP from 2025 to 2031, significantly more than the rest of the G7, many of which are increasing their deficit over this time period.
The UK is also projected to have the lowest annual borrowing in the G7 in 2031, and the longest maturity of debt, locking in lower rates for longer.
Asked if the UK was one of the countries the IMF was telling to reduce borrowing, Tenreyro said that the country had begun the process already and should "stay the course".
The head of the IMF has previously called on the world's advanced economies to cut borrowing and reduce debt levels.
The reversal of downgrades to economic forecasts made at the start of the US-Iran war, mean the UK is expected to have the second-fasted growing economy in the G7 along with Germany.
But growth is estimated to slow in 2027 to 1.2% due to higher energy prices and long-term interest rates weighing on household spending and business investment.
Healey acknowledged that wars in the Middle East and Europe were "hitting people in the UK and around the world", but added that "Britain's economy is showing strong international resilience".
When the economy is growing, businesses tend to invest more, more jobs are created and people, on average, tend to feel better off. The opposite can occur if the economy stagnates or shrinks.
Maike Currie, head of personal finance for Pension Bee, told the BBC the IMF's report "does give the chancellor a little bit of breathing space" but that "it doesn't mean that families are feeling better off just yet and I don't think it is a gamechanger".
Economists have suggested Healey faces having to find £35bn to avoid cuts to public spending while meeting defence promises in his first Budget.
On Tuesday, the Resolution Foundation called on the chancellor to make "make repairs" to the public finances, but said well-targeted support was needed for those "struggling to heat their homes".
"The challenge of continuing to bring down borrowing must be paired with the pressing need for fresh cost of living support to help families facing a difficult winter ahead," the think tank said.
Andrew Griffith, Conservative shadow chancellor, said if Healey "reaches for more tax rises" in his Budget, "he is choosing slower growth and working people will pay for it".
Burnham has pledged to create "good growth in every postcode" as part of his plans to giving nations and regions more control, but his strategy has faced criticism inside his own party.
The IMF said households are likely to continue feeling the pinch of rising prices, with inflation expected to average 3.3% this year and remain above the Bank of England's 2% target in 2027 at 2.8%.
The Bank itself has predicted inflation could rise above 4% at the beginning of next year - making it more likely that interest rates will rise.
Healey is expected to meet with other finance ministers at the IMF's annual meeting in Bangkok, Thailand, on Tuesday to discuss how the economic impact of the Middle East and European conflicts could be limited.
The IMF said the global economy had shown a "remarkable capacity to absorb shocks" not just from the current Middle East conflict, but also from the Covid pandemic and Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
description: The IMF report comes as final preparations are being made to the first Budget under Prime Minister Andy Burham.

title: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel kill five people on Mexico’s Pacific coast
content_c:
At least five people have died after Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel pummelled Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing flooding that downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and inundated homes.
Simon claimed the life of a 71-year-old man who died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo in the southern state of Guerrero, governor Evelyn Salgado said at a press conference.
The storm also damaged infrastructure and homes in the state’s coastal towns, including the major seaport of Acapulco, she said.
Tropical Storm Rachel is blamed for the deaths of four members of one family, including two children, whose bodies were found on the outskirts of the city of Ensenada in Baja California, the state’s prosecutor’s office reported.
Five more people remained missing, while security forces used helicopters to rescue 32 people, prosecutors said. Baja governor Marina del Pilar said officials were helping more than 50 people in temporary shelters.
Simon did not make landfall and, after weakening to category two on the five-point Saffir-Simpson scale, was moving away from the coast, authorities said. A rain alert remained in place.
The National Hurricane Center in Miami said heavy rainfall associated with Simon in west-central Mexico over the next few days might still produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides.
Officials warned waves of up to five metres high were still expected in some coastal areas. Flooding and landslides had already hit communities close to rivers and streams in the states of Michoacan and Colima.
The El Niño phenomenon, characterised by rising water temperatures in the Pacific, is fuelling a more intense hurricanes this season in the region.
Meteorologists say the 2026-27 El Niño, which causes global changes in winds and rainfall as well as erratic weather conditions, is certain to be the biggest ever recorded. Scientists now also think human-caused global heating is making El Niños more intense.
With Agence France-Presse and Associated Press

title: Mahmood orders urgent security review after killing of Ann Widdecombe
content_c:
Security arrangements for high-profile public figures including politicians and members of the royal family are to be urgently reviewed after the killing of Ann Widdecombe, the home secretary has said.
Shabana Mahmood said former MPs, party leaders who are not MPs, peers, former members of devolved parliaments and party spokespeople will also be offered police support.
The UK’s protective security system will be re-examined to combat the growing risks of terrorism, extremism and state threats, as well as harassment and intimidation, Mahmood said.
The review will be carried out by Sir Stephen Lovegrove, a former UK national security adviser, who will look at whether current security arrangements ensure there is adequate protection for those most at risk.
This includes high-profile individuals such as members of the royal family, government ministers, MPs, locally elected representatives and other prominent individuals in British politics. His review will not include an assessment of individual cases.
Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokesperson, was found dead on 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.
Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with Widdecombe’s murder. He is also accused of “online reconnaissance” of prominent people and institutions, travelling to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage’s home in south London on 19 April 2025 and trying to break into it 15 months before Widdecombe was killed.
Addressing the Commons, Mahmood said that, regardless of the outcome of the investigation into an attempted break-in at Farage’s home, it is “clear there is insufficient protection for those who serve”.
“I can therefore announce today that I will expand, with immediate effect, police support to political figures who are not currently members of parliament,” she said. “This will include former members of parliament, peers and party spokespeople, giving them access to a named police officer, as well as help with wider security measures.
Mahmood added: “Today I also announce an independent root-and-branch review of the protective security provided by the state to those in public life. We can defeat those who mean us harm, but we are strongest when we act together.
 “In a more dangerous world, we are faced by threats from without and within that target our democracy and our way of life. In response, we are adapting and strengthening our defences.
 “As ever, I commend the work of the police and our security services, who labour in silence to keep us safe. And I’m sure the whole house joins me in offering thanks to them for that vital life-saving work.”
Lovegrove will look at how existing security is provided, whether funding and other measures are being used effectively and proportionately, and how decision-making can be more consistent in response to threat and risk.
Robert Buckland is conducting a separate review into the murder of Sir David Amess MP, which will consider the security of MPs in their constituencies.
In May’s local elections the Electoral Commission found that 55% of all candidates experienced some form of harassment and intimidation, as did the same proportion of candidates at the 2024 general election.

title: US: Man killed in Six Flags roller coaster incident
content_c:
US: Man killed in Six Flags roller coaster incident
October 13, 2026
One person has died and several others were injured in an incident on Monday involving a roller coaster at a Six Flags theme park in the United States.
The incident occurred at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24 kilometers) northwest of Atlanta.
Witnesses told local media outlets that they saw a man fall from the ride.
"I cannot imagine the horror the patrons and employees witnessed today, and my heart aches for the family who lost a loved one," said Lisa Cupid, chair of the Cobb County Board of Commissioners.
Six Flags temporary closes 9 roller coasters
Following the incident in Georgia, Six Flags temporarily closed nine roller coasters across six amusement parks.
According to a park spokesperson, similar attractions were closed across their parks "out of an abundance of caution" following the incident at Six Flags Over Georgia.
This comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California announced it would retire its famous X2 roller coaster amid lawsuits alleging the ride caused serious brain injuries.
What do we know about the roller coaster?
Althought the park did not identify the ride involved in Monday's incident, local media showed passengers being evacuated from the Goliath coaster.
Built in 2006, Goliath can reach speeds of 113 km/h (70 mph) and a maximum height of 61 meters (200 feet).
According to the theme park's website, riders "navigate through razor-sharp turns and soar over colossal hills."
Monday's death would be at least the seventh to occur at the Georgia theme park, according to the Doan Law Firm, which focuses on amusement park accidents.
That includes one 2006 incident when a man had a likely heart attack while riding the same roller coaster, Goliath.

title: Wein in Deutschland: Ernte so gering wie seit 2010 nicht mehr
content_c:
Lese abgeschlossen Weinernte so gering wie seit 2010 nicht mehr
Die Weinlese in Deutschland fällt in diesem Jahr voraussichtlich so niedrig aus wie zuletzt 2010. Das Deutsche Weininstitut (DWI) geht in einer ersten Prognose davon aus, dass die Menge rund 20 Prozent unter dem zehnjährigen Durchschnitt von 8,7 Millionen Hektolitern liegt.
2010 waren es 7,1 Millionen Hektoliter und im vergangenen Jahr 7,7 Millionen, wie DWI-Sprecher Ernst Büscher zum Ende der Lese sagte. Bis auf einige Ausnahmen – vor allem im Anbaugebiet Saale-Unstrut – sei die Lese fast überall abgeschlossen.
Viele Trauben seien bei dem extrem trockenen und sonnenreichen Sommer klein geblieben. »Die Winzerinnen und Winzer hierzulande gehen zwar von vergleichsweise kleinen Gesamtmengen, aber von Spitzenqualitäten aus.«
Die Ertragslage variierte innerhalb der Regionen je nach Alter der Reben und Wasserspeicherkraft der Böden sehr stark, wie Büscher sagte. »Insbesondere ältere Reben haben sich in den letzten Jahren an die zunehmende Trockenheit in den Weinregionen angepasst und dank ihrer tiefen Wurzeln die diesjährige Dürre erstaunlich gut überstanden.« Jüngere Weinberge und Anlagen auf leichten Böden hätten dagegen sichtbar unter der Wasserknappheit gelitten. »Sie mussten, wenn möglich, bewässert werden.«
Klimawandel verändert Weinanbau
Im ostfranzösischen Burgund hatte die Lese für den Schaumwein Crémant in diesem Jahr so früh begonnen wie noch nie in der Geschichte der Region. Wie stark der menschengemachte Klimawandel den Weinbau verändert, zeigt eine Untersuchung des Klimahistorikers Thomas Labbé in der Fachzeitschrift »Climate of the Past«. Er wertete Erntedaten der burgundischen Stadt Beaune von 1354 bis heute aus. Die Reihe umfasst mehr als 670 Jahre und offenbart laut dem Forscher eine »Explosion« extremer Jahre.
Während sich Phasen mit großer Hitze und verfrühten Ernten zwischen 1354 und 1719 im Schnitt alle 17 Jahre wiederholten, lagen sie von 1720 bis 1987 durchschnittlich 53 Jahre auseinander. Seit 1988 haben sich die Abstände drastisch verkürzt: Extreme Hitze trat seitdem alle fünf Jahre auf. Im 21. Jahrhundert registrierte der Historiker bereits zehn solcher Jahre – statistisch entspricht das einem Rhythmus von etwa zweieinhalb Jahren.
Die Weinlese in Saale-Unstrut fiel in diesem Jahr zusammen mit der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt. Die eine fürchtet sich vor der AfD, der andere schimpft über »die Wichser in Berlin«: Lesen Sie hier , was Winzerinnen und Winzer von Bürokratie und Klimawandel und von Arbeitskräften aus der Ukraine erzählen – und von der Angst, nach der Wahl isoliert zu sein.
description: Der trockene und heiße Sommer war für die deutschen Weinanbaugebiete Fluch und Segen zugleich. Das Deutsche Weininstitut rechnet mit einem wenig ertragreichen Jahrgang, hat aber auch gute Nachrichten.

Im ostfranzösischen Burgund hatte die Lese für den Schaumwein Crémant in diesem Jahr so früh begonnen wie noch nie in der Geschichte der Region. Wie stark der menschengemachte Klimawandel den Weinbau verändert, zeigt eine Untersuchung des Klimahistorikers Thomas Labbé in der Fachzeitschrift »Climate of the Past«. Er wertete Erntedaten der burgundischen Stadt Beaune von 1354 bis heute aus. Die Reihe umfasst mehr als 670 Jahre und offenbart laut dem Forscher eine »Explosion« extremer Jahre.
Während sich Phasen mit großer Hitze und verfrühten Ernten zwischen 1354 und 1719 im Schnitt alle 17 Jahre wiederholten, lagen sie von 1720 bis 1987 durchschnittlich 53 Jahre auseinander. Seit 1988 haben sich die Abstände drastisch verkürzt: Extreme Hitze trat seitdem alle fünf Jahre auf. Im 21. Jahrhundert registrierte der Historiker bereits zehn solcher Jahre – statistisch entspricht das einem Rhythmus von etwa zweieinhalb Jahren.
Die Weinlese in Saale-Unstrut fiel in diesem Jahr zusammen mit der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt. Die eine fürchtet sich vor der AfD, der andere schimpft über »die Wichser in Berlin«: Lesen Sie hier , was Winzerinnen und Winzer von Bürokratie und Klimawandel und von Arbeitskräften aus der Ukraine erzählen – und von der Angst, nach der Wahl isoliert zu sein.

title: Marktbericht: Anleger warten ab
content_c:
DAX seitwärts erwartet Anleger warten ab
Zum Handelsstart dürften sich die DAX-Anleger mit neuen Engagements erst einmal bedeckt halten. Weiterhin hohe Ölpreise, aber auch das Warten auf den Beginn der US-Berichtssaison, sorgen für Zurückhaltung.
Der DAX wird am Morgen in ersten Berechnungen leicht unter dem Vortagesniveau erwartet. Zu Wochenbeginn hatte der deutsche Leitindex noch knapp 0,8 Prozent zugelegt auf 25.277 Punkte - und dabei auch einem Anstieg der Ölpreise getrotzt. Aber die Risiken bleiben hoch, denn ein Ende der hohen Energiepreis scheint weiter nicht in Sicht. Im Gegenteil: Der Angriff der jemenitischen Huthi-Rebellen auf die saudi-arabische Hauptstadt Riad deutet eher auf eine weitere Eskalation hin.
Neben der geostrategisch schwierigen Weltlage blicken die Anleger zudem auf den Beginn der US-Berichtssaison, die vor dem Handelsstart an der Wall Street mit den Quartalszahlen der großen Banken startet. Vier der sechs großen US Häuser, JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo und die führende Investmentbank Goldman Sachs, öffnen ihre Bücher.
Zudem berichten auch die im Leitindex Dow Jones enthaltenen Großkonzerne Johnson & Johnson, ein Gesundheitsriese, sowie der größte Krankenversicherer des Landes, UnitedHealth.
Die Vorgaben aus Asien sind derweil schwach, die Märkte in Fernost litten unter den geopolitischen Spannungen und schwachen US-Technologiewerten. "Man kann mit Fug und Recht behaupten, dass der japanische Aktienmarkt heute von dem Abwärtstrend bei den US-Halbleiteraktien beeinflusst wird", sagte Maki Sawada, Strategin bei Nomura Securities. Der Nikkei-Index verliert über zwei Prozent.
Der Internationale Währungsfonds (IWF) setzt derweil seine Wirtschaftsprognose für Deutschland und die Weltwirtschaft hoch. Der IWF rechnet nun damit, dass das deutsche Bruttoinlandsprodukt (BIP) im laufenden Jahr um 1,3 Prozent wächst, wie aus dem heute beim IWF-Jahrestreffen in Bangkok veröffentlichten Weltwirtschaftsausblick hervorging.
Das sind 0,6 Prozentpunkte mehr als noch im Juli prognostiziert und stimmt mit der Prognose der Bundesregierung überein. Auch seine Erwartung für das globale Wirtschaftsleistung hob der IWF leicht um 0,1 Prozentpunkte auf 3,1 Prozent an.
Der IWF rechnet nun damit, dass sich das weltweite Wirtschaftswachstum etwas weniger verlangsamt als zuvor erwartet, da die Industrieländer sich trotz der seit dem Iran-Krieg gestiegenen Energiepreise widerstandsfähig gezeigt hätten. "Die Weltwirtschaft hat sich als widerstandsfähig erwiesen, doch diese Widerstandsfähigkeit steht unter Druck, und die Risiken für das Wachstum sind eher nach unten gerichtet", gab IWF-Chefökonomin Silvana Tenreyro an.
Am Rohölmarkt bleiben die Preise nach den Angriffen auf den Flughafen der saudi-arabischen Hauptstadt Riad hoch und stiegen in der Spitze auf ein Zwei-Wochen-Hoch. Nordsee-Rohöl Brent und US-Leichtöl WTI verteuerten sich zwischen 1,3 und 1,5 Prozent auf rund 106 und 93 Dollar je Fass. Aktuell stehen die Notierungen nur leicht darunter.
Nach der Ausweitung der Angriffe der Huthi-Rebellen hoben die Analysten von Goldman Sachs daher ihre Prognose für den Brent-Preis für Dezember von 85 auf 90 Dollar pro Fass an. Der Energiesektor gehörte wegen der anziehenden Ölpreise zu den stärksten Branchen im S&P 500
Vor dem Start in die US-Bilanzsaison haben sich US-Anleger zu Wochenbeginn vorsichtig gezeigt. Der US-Standardwerteindex Dow Jones gewann am Montag 0,4 Prozent auf 51.851 Punkte. Der technologielastige Nasdaq gab 0,4 Prozent auf 27.246 Zähler nach und der breit gefasste S&P 500 schloss kaum verändert bei 7.807 Stellen.
"Die großen Themen, die es in der Berichtssaison zu beobachten gilt, sind, wie Unternehmen KI einsetzen und davon profitieren", sagte Clark Bellin von Bellwether Wealth. Zudem sei wichtig, ob sie ihre Preissetzungsmacht beibehalten oder erhöhen und wie sie mit den gestiegenen Kreditkosten umgehen könnten.
Auf die Stimmung drückten am Montag erneut anziehende Ölpreise und die unsichere Lage im Nahen Osten. Auch Chipaktien tendierten schwächer. Zudem hielten sich Investoren wegen fehlender Impulse vom Anleihemarkt zurück, da der US-Rentenmarkt wegen des Feiertags Columbus Day geschlossen blieb.
Die Aktienhändler blickten zudem mit Sorge auf die jüngst auf ein 24-Jahres-Hoch gestiegenen Renditen, da hohe Energiepreise die Inflationssorgen schürten. Die Aussicht auf steigende Unternehmensgewinne und die Hoffnung, dass die Fed kurzfristige Zinserhöhungen vermeiden könnte, hatten vergangene Woche die drei wichtigsten Börsenindizes ins Plus gehievt.

title: Ukraine und USA in der Krise: Was folgt auf den Diesel-Deal mit Russland?
content_c:
Ukraine-Krieg: Trumps Diesel-Deal mit Russland und die Folgen
12. Oktober 2026
Der Diesel-Deal zwischen US-Präsident Donald Trump und Russlands Staatschef Wladimir Putin sorgt in der Ukraine für Verärgerung. Moskau darf damit russischen Dieselkraftstoff in die Weltmärkte liefern. Dies sei eine Reaktion darauf, dass Kyjiw den Forderungen Washingtons nicht nachkomme, die Angriffe auf Raffinerien in Russland zu stoppen, schreibt die US-amerikanischen Nachrichtenseite Axios. Trump erklärte zudem, es sei für die Ukraine an der Zeit, "einen neuen Führer zu bekommen, der einen Deal machen könnte".
Die Vereinbarung über den Dieselverkauf wurde verkündet, während Gespräche zwischen ukrainischen, amerikanischen und europäischen Vertretern in Miami liefen. "Ich glaube, unser Team wird lediglich als Deckmantel missbraucht. Das ist definitiv nicht fair", sagte der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj kurze Zeit später vor Journalisten und bezeichnete Trumps Beschluss als "eine schwache Entscheidung starker Partner".
Vom Oval Office nach Miami
Für Kyjiw ist das nicht die erste Krise im Verhältnis zur Trump-Administration. Im Februar 2025 warf Trump im Oval Office Selenskyj vor, er habe "im Moment keine Karten". Auf den Eklat im Weißen Haus folgte ein Stopp der Waffenlieferungen und des Austauschs geheimdienstlicher Informationen. Die US-Sondergesandten Steve Witkoff und Jared Kushner sollen laut Medienberichten während der Gespräche in Miami erneut mit einem Informations-Stopp gedroht und das mit den ukrainischen Angriffen auf russische Raffinerien begründet haben. US-Vertreter bestritten diese Darstellung.
Dennoch ähnele die aktuelle Situation dem damaligen Streit im Weißen Haus, sagt Mychajlo Hontschar vom ukrainischen Zentrum für Globale Studien "Strategie XXI" im DW-Gespräch. Es gebe aber keinen Grund für die Ukrainer, jetzt in Panik zu geraten. "Auch im vergangenen Jahr gab es Drohungen und Unterbrechungen der Geheimdienstinformationen sowie Lieferengpässen bei den Waffen. Dann erkannten die Amerikaner, wie sehr es ihnen selbst schadet, und nahmen widerwillig alles wieder auf."
Sucht Trump einen "Sündenbock"?
Alle von der DW befragten Experten sehen einen Zusammenhang zwischen Trumps Drohgebärden gegenüber der Ukraine und den Zwischenwahlen in den USA am 3. November. Bei den Midterms werden alle Sitze des Repräsentantenhauses und ein turnusmäßiger Teil des Senats neu gewählt. Iwan Us vom Nationalen Institut für strategische Studien in Kyjiw erwartet eine krachende Niederlage der Republikaner. Hauptgrund dafür seien die hohen Treibstoffpreise.
"Donald Trump will mit aller Macht davon ablenken, dass die hohen Preise mit seinem Iran-Krieg und den Problemen in der Straße von Hormus zusammenhängen. Dafür braucht er einen Sündenbock. Und er hat entschieden, dass es die Ukraine ist", betont der Experte.
Mychajlo Hontschar sieht in Trumps Deal mit Putin vor allem Vorteile für Russland. "Dieses ganze Dieselgeschäft wirkt wie eine verkappte Bitte Putins an Trump, Einfluss auf die Ukraine zu nehmen." Hontschar bringt die Vereinbarung auch mit einem möglichen Verkauf der Auslandsbeteiligungen des russischen Ölkonzerns Lukoil in Verbindung. Laut der New York Times gehören zu den potenziellen Käufern dieser Beteiligungen Investoren aus Trumps Umfeld.
Wie lässt sich die Krise bewältigen?
Oleksandr Krajew vom ukrainischen Thinktank "Ukrainisches Prisma" warnt vor drastischen Schritten. "Wenn wir beleidigt die Tür zuschlagen, wird uns das ganz sicher nicht helfen. Dann werden die Sicherheitsunterstützung und die Geheimdienstinformationen vom Tisch sein. Das können wir uns nicht leisten. Es mag schwierig sein, manchmal auch widerwärtig, aber wir müssen den Kontakt zu den Amerikanern aufrechterhalten", findet der Experte. Parallel dazu könne die Ukraine mit Deutschland, Dänemark, Großbritannien und Frankreich dafür sorgen, dass Lieferungen von russischem Dieselkraftstoff "einfach unrealistisch" würden. Schließlich müssten die Tanker durch Hoheitsgewässer dieser Länder in die USA fahren und die Partner hätten schon erklärt, dies nicht zulassen zu wollen.
Ivan Us rät, scharfer Rhetorik nicht zu viel Bedeutung beizumessen. "Man kann öffentlich sagen, was man will, Hauptsache, man macht weiter wie bisher", lautet seine Einschätzung zum möglichen Verhältnis zwischen Kyjiw und Washington. Die ukrainische Diplomatie sollte mit den US-Republikanern und der MAGA-Bewegung zusammenarbeiten. Dort werde Trumps Vereinbarung mit Putin bereits kritisiert und der Verdacht geäußert, Russland könne mit dem Geld aus dem Dieselgeschäft den Iran unterstützen.
Us schließt zudem nicht aus, dass Trumps Entscheidung vor Gericht angefochten wird. Der republikanische Senator Tom Tillis sagte im US-Sender NBC, der Präsident verstoße wahrscheinlich gegen das Gesetz aus dem Jahr 2022, das den Import von russischem Öl und weiteren Energieträgern verbiete.
Die US-Drohungen, die Ukraine von geheimdienstlichen Informationen oder Waffen abzuschneiden, hält Iwan Us ohnehin für "Angstmacherei" im Vorfeld der Wahlen. "Die USA geben solche Erklärungen nicht ab, um etwas zu unternehmen, sondern um die Märkte glauben zu lassen, dass sie nun Druck ausüben werden, und die Preise sinken", so Us.
Was ändert sich ab dem 3. November?
Die drei Experten sind sich einig, dass Kyjiw die Lage bis nach den US-Wahlen aussitzen sollte. Oleksandr Krajew ist überzeugt, dass Trump nach den Wahlen in dieser Angelegenheit nachgeben könnte. Denn die Ukraine im Stich zu lassen würde bedeuten, Schwäche gegenüber China zu zeigen, das die Situation um Taiwan genau im Blick habe.
Mychajlo Hontschar weist darauf hin, dass Trumps Deal mit Putin bereits von Republikanern im Senat und im Repräsentantenhaus kritisiert werde. Zudem habe der Kongressabgeordnete Brian Fitzpatrick einen nach dem ehemaligen US-Präsidenten Ronald Reagan benannten parteiübergreifenden Gesetzentwurf initiiert, um den Kauf von russischem Öl zu blockieren. "Trotz aller Drohungen und vielleicht sogar einiger Versuche, vorübergehende Maßnahmen gegen Kyjiw zu erlassen, ist es unwahrscheinlich, dass Trump noch weiter gehen wird. Die Lage sollte man nicht in apokalyptischen Tönen darstellen", so Hontschar. Zudem sorge Trump mit seinem Druck nur für einen noch engeren Schulterschluss zwischen der Ukraine und ihren europäischen Partnern.
Adaption aus dem Ukrainischen: Markian Ostaptschuk
description: Donald Trump will den Kauf russischen Diesels erlauben, was im In- und Ausland kritisiert wird. Was ist der Grund für die Entscheidung des US-Präsidenten und was soll die Ukraine tun? Die DW hat mit Experten gesprochen.

Zudem sorge Trump mit seinem Druck nur für einen noch engeren Schulterschluss zwischen der Ukraine und ihren europäischen Partnern.

title: Минулої доби росіяни атакували на семи напрямках, на Покровському – 29 разів
content_c:
Минулої доби росіяни атакували на семи напрямках, на Покровському – 29 разів
За даними Генштабу, протягом 12 жовтня на фронті відбулося 203 бойові зіткнення, зокрема росіяни здійснили 29 атак на Покровському напрямку та 20 – на Південно-Слобожанському.
Джерело: Генштаб
Деталі: Загалом протягом минулої доби зафіксовано 203 бойові зіткнення.
На Північно-Слобожанському і Курському напрямках минулої доби агресор здійснив 49 обстрілів позицій українських військ і населених пунктів.
На Південно-Слобожанському напрямку українські підрозділи відбили 20 атак противника. Загарбники намагалися просунутися у районах населених пунктів Стариця, Ізбицьке, Вовчанські Хутори, Зибино та в бік Захарівки, Варварівки, Радьківки, Дорошівки.
На Куп'янському напрямку ворог штурмових дій не проводив.
Спроби вклинитися в українську оборону відбито на Лиманському напрямку, де окупанти шість разів атакували в районах населених пунктів Колодязі та Лиман.
На Слов'янському та Краматорському напрямках противник штурмових дій не проводив.
На Костянтинівському напрямку зафіксовано 15 атак. Загарбники вели наступальні дії в районах населених пунктів Костянтинівка, Софіївка, Довга Балка та у бік Миколайпілля.
Двадцять дев'ять атак здійснив ворог на Покровському напрямку. Окупанти намагалися просунутися у бік населених пунктів Грузьке, Торецьке, Вільне, Кучерів Яр, Добропілля, Світле, Мирне, Сергіївка та у районі Молодецького.
На Олександрівському напрямку ворог один раз атакував у бік Тернового.
На Гуляйпільському напрямку противник 12 разів намагався просунутися у районах населених пунктів Різдвянка, Тернове та в бік населених пунктів Нове Запоріжжя, Косівцеве, Гірке, Воздвижівка, Придорожнє.
На Оріхівському та Придніпровському напрямках окупанти штурмових дій не проводили.
На Волинському та Поліському напрямках ознак формування наступальних угруповань ворога не виявлено.

title: Ассія Ахат розкрила подробиці кумівства з Нікітіним і Горбачовою: як живе її 21-річна похресниця
content_c:
Ассія Ахат розкрила подробиці кумівства з Нікітіним і Горбачовою: як живе її 21-річна похресниця
Скрипалька Ассія Ахат дотепер підтримує музичні амбіції 21-річної Поліни.
Українська скрипалька та співачка Ассія Ахат розповіла про стосунки з 21-річною похресницею Поліною — донькою продюсера Юрія Нікітіна та співачки Ольги Горбачової.
В інтерв’ю проєкту «Наодинці з Гламуром» артистка зізналася, що досі підтримує зв’язок із донькою колишнього подружжя. Попри відстань, вони знаходять можливість бачитися за кордоном.
Так, Поліна приїжджає в гості до зіркової хрещеної, а та відвідує її виступи та підтримує музичні починання дівчини. Нині 21-річна Поліна розвивається як артистка й прагне побудувати кар’єру у США.
«Я хрещена мати першої доньки у Юрія Нікітіна та Ольги Горбачової. Ми теж підтримуємо зв’язок. а Поліна дуже класна артистка. Так, Поля приїжджає. Коли я у Нью-Йорку, ми зустрічаємося. І приходжу на її виступи», — поділилася Ассія у розмові з Анною Севастьяновою.
Також співачка розповіла про дружбу з колегою Іриною Білик. За словами Ахат, вони спілкуються та зустрічаються як в Україні, так і в Америці. Артистки добре знають одна одну й залишаються джерелом підтримки.

title: Украинские города могут остаться без воды: какой сценарий наиболее вероятен этой зимой
content_c:
Длительные отключения электроэнергии могут повлиять на водоснабжение в украинских городах, значительная часть которых может перейти на почасовую подачу воды. Ведь автономные источники питания способны поддерживать работу сетей, однако давления может не хватить для подачи воды на верхние этажи многоэтажных домов. Об этом рассказал директор Ассоциации «Укрводоканалекология» Александр Шкин.
По его словам, стабильность водоснабжения напрямую зависит от наличия электроэнергии.
Среди положительных моментов — в большинстве городов резервные источники питания обеспечивают подачу воды в сеть как минимум на несколько часов в сутки. Проблема возникает с подачей воды в многоэтажках, ведь мощности резервных источников недостаточно для поддержания необходимого давления в высотных зданиях.
Другими словами, вода в сети будет, но жители верхних этажей могут не получать её без дополнительной работы насосов.
Киев, по словам эксперта, требует отдельной оценки из-за мощных насосных станций и особенностей городской системы водоснабжения. Для других городов базовым сценарием может стать периодическая подача воды в течение суток.
Шкинь подтвердил, что в случае длительных проблем с электроснабжением в Украине могут вводиться графики подачи воды. Их продолжительность будет зависеть, в частности, от возможности подвозить топливо к генераторам и необходимости периодически останавливать автономные установки.
Накануне заместитель генерального директора коммунального предприятия «Киевводоканал» Сергей Горкуценко заявил, что в случае сохранения нынешней интенсивности российских обстрелов и перебоев с электроснабжением жители Киева могут полностью остаться без воды в кранах, а столица столкнётся с риском масштабной эпидемиологической катастрофы из-за остановки канализации.
Хотя питьевую воду населению гарантированно будут подвозить специальными автоцистернами и в емкостях, ситуация с подачей воды непосредственно в квартиры остается критической. Однако главная проблема — даже не отсутствие воды в водопроводе, а невозможность отвода стоков из-за ограниченного электроснабжения.

title: Реактивні шахеди атакували Львів уночі, горять будинки. Атака Росії триває по всій Україні
content_c:
Реактивні шахеди атакували Львів уночі, горять будинки. Атака Росії триває по всій Україні
  - Author, Відділ новин
  - Role, ВВС News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 3 хв
Реактивні шахеди атакували Львів після 5 години ранку. У місті було чути роботу ППО та кілька гучних вибухів. Дронова атака на Україну тривала з вечора усю ніч – у Харкові тіла трьох загиблих деблокували з-під завалів багатоповерхівки.
Мер Львова Андрій Садовий повідомив про два дрони, які були над містом.
Згодом керівник області Максим Козицький повідомив, що один збитий безпілотник впав на житловий будинок у селі Муроване у передмісті Львова. Він каже, що горять три будинки і пошкоджені три автомобілі. Інформації про постраждалих поки що немає.
Уламки іншого дрона знайшли на одній з вулиць Львова, каже Козицький.
За даними Повітряних сил, реактивні шахеди запускали на Львів через Одещину, Вінниччину, Хмельниччину і Тернопільщину.
Начальник Рівненської ОВА Олександр Коваль розповів про удари по Сарненщині. За його словами, росіяни атакували підприємство, що не працює, проте була пошкоджена інфраструктура, гуртожитки та житлові будинки.
Раніше від удару дрона у Івано-Франківську на заході України загинули троє людей.
Терор реактивними шахедами на Україну, а особливо на Київ, розпочався наприкінці серпня. З того часу такі дрони практично цілодобово атакують столицю.
Аналітики вказували, що ближче до зими росіяни зуміють діставати такими дронами і захід України. Останніми тижнями реактивні шахеди вже постійно атакують Волинь, Рівненщину, Тернопільщину, Прикарпаття, а тепер і Львів.
Реактивні шахеди розвивають швидкість у понад 500 км на годину та летять на значній висоті, через що звичними мобільними вогневими групами або перехоплювачами їх збивати складно.
Попередні удари: загиблі у Києві та Харкові
Напередодні ввечері Росія атакувала Київ ракетами та дронами. Через удар шахедом по багатоповерхівці загинули двоє людей. Одну із загиблих знайшли у згорілій автівці біля власного будинку.
Крім того, як передає Суспільне, відомо про 11 постраждалих. Пошкоджені кілька житлових будинків, згоріли дев'ять автомобілів. Один із ударів прийшовся по складській будівлі в Деснянському районі.

content:
Реактивні шахеди атакували Львів уночі, горять будинки. Атака Росії триває по всій Україні
  - Author, Відділ новин
  - Role, ВВС News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 3 хв
Реактивні шахеди атакували Львів після 5 години ранку. У місті було чути роботу ППО та кілька гучних вибухів. Дронова атака на Україну тривала з вечора усю ніч – у Харкові тіла трьох загиблих деблокували з-під завалів багатоповерхівки.
Мер Львова Андрій Садовий повідомив про два дрони, які були над містом.
Згодом керівник області Максим Козицький повідомив, що один збитий безпілотник впав на житловий будинок у селі Муроване у передмісті Львова. Він каже, що горять три будинки і пошкоджені три автомобілі. Інформації про постраждалих поки що немає.
Уламки іншого дрона знайшли на одній з вулиць Львова, каже Козицький.
За даними Повітряних сил, реактивні шахеди запускали на Львів через Одещину, Вінниччину, Хмельниччину і Тернопільщину.
Начальник Рівненської ОВА Олександр Коваль розповів про удари по Сарненщині. За його словами, росіяни атакували підприємство, що не працює, проте була пошкоджена інфраструктура, гуртожитки та житлові будинки.
Раніше від удару дрона у Івано-Франківську на заході України загинули троє людей.
Терор реактивними шахедами на Україну, а особливо на Київ, розпочався наприкінці серпня. З того часу такі дрони практично цілодобово атакують столицю.
Аналітики вказували, що ближче до зими росіяни зуміють діставати такими дронами і захід України. Останніми тижнями реактивні шахеди вже постійно атакують Волинь, Рівненщину, Тернопільщину, Прикарпаття, а тепер і Львів.
Реактивні шахеди розвивають швидкість у понад 500 км на годину та летять на значній висоті, через що звичними мобільними вогневими групами або перехоплювачами їх збивати складно.

title: One dead and several hurt after rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
content_c:
One dead and several hurt after rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
- Published
One person has died and several others were injured after an incident on a rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, an amusement park in the US state of Georgia.
The Cobb County Police Department said it was investigating the fatality at the park, about 15 miles (24km) from Atlanta, according to the BBC's news partner CBS.
Police did not specify what ride was involved, but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, with riders being helped off by workers.
Six Flags Over Georgia said it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones."
Officials have not said how the person was killed. The BBC has contacted local police and fire authorities, as well as park officials.
Witnesses told local media they saw a man ejected from the ride, accounts that the BBC has not verified.
Local outlet 11Alive quoted, external a witness saying the man fell from the rollercoaster on to the roof of a haunted house attraction.
A park spokesperson said in a statement that its team and local authorities had responded immediately, and they were co-operating on an investigation into the incident.
Mableton Mayor Michael Owens said the city's public safety director was co-ordinating with local police and park security on the situation.
The Goliath ride opened in 2006, and it has an elevation of 200ft (60m), a 170ft plunge, a 540-degree spiral, and a speed of up to 70mph (112km/h), according to the park website. On its "thrill scale", Six Flags ranks Goliath at level four out of five.
Six Flags is the largest amusement park operator in North America, with 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resorts across Canada, the US and Mexico.
The incident comes just weeks after one of its parks in southern California announced it would close the popular X2 roller coaster after more than 100 people alleged brain injuries from the ride.
Six Flags said the ride had passed a range of safety tests, but that it had decided to retire it because it was "the right thing to do".

title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs
content_c:
Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs
- Published
Political figures who are not currently MPs will be given police support, the home secretary has announced.
Shabana Mahmood told MPs there was "insufficient protection" for those serving in public life and that the new announcement will cover peers, former MPs and party spokespeople.
She also announced an urgent, independent review of security arrangements for high-profile figures including politicians and royals.
It comes three months after Reform UK spokeswoman and former Conservative MP Ann Widdecombe was found dead at her home in Devon, having been hit on the head with a hammer 21 times as she ate lunch.
Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with her murder, and he was also charged with preparing acts of terror against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.
Kerry is alleged to have carried out research on prominent targets over a period of two years, including trying to gain entry into Farage's London home.
Speaking in the Commons on Monday, Mahmood said that "robust debate and criticism are part of this job - threats, abuse and violence are not."
She did not elaborate on what the support would involve, but told MPs it would include access to a named police officer and help with wider security measures.
The safety of politicians has been a prominent issue in recent years, following the murders of Conservative MP Sir David Amess in 2021 and Labour MP Jo Cox in 2016.
"We owe it to them and to everyone who believes in a fair and open country to ensure that those who serve at all levels receive the protection they deserve," Mahmood added.
The "root and branch" independent review into security arrangements will be led by former national security advisor Stephen Lovegrove, and will look into "physical threats, online risks and the dangers posed within our more polarised society".
Mahmood confirmed that the review will report within six months, and build on the existing work of Sir Robert Buckland, who is leading a separate review into the murder of Sir David.
In response, shadow home secretary Chris Philp welcomed the extension of protective measures, saying threats to elected representatives are threats to democracy.
Reform UK's home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf welcomed the review, but added: "It is disappointing that it took the murder of one of our colleagues, countless threats towards our party spokespeople and months of campaigning from Reform UK to make this government take action."
Reform has in recent months accused the government of a "dereliction of duty" over Farage's taxpayer-funded security, claiming it had previously been "downgraded" - a charge that the Home Office has said is "categorically untrue".
Decisions over the security of current MPs and members of the House of Lords are made by the House of Parliament's security team.
There is a separate, independent committee, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (Ravec), to deal with high-profile political candidates, which is staffed by officials from the Home Office, the Cabinet Office, and the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
The Jo Cox Foundation welcomed the home secretary's announcement but said "strengthening physical security" alone was not enough.
"We must also tackle the root causes - including online harms and education - to prevent future attacks," its chief executive Olivia Field said in a statement on X.
According to data released to the BBC in April, the number of alleged offences against MPs have increased year-on-year, with 976 recorded in 2025, compared to 364 in 2019.
MPs reported 4,064 crimes to the Met's Parliamentary Liaison Team between 2019 and 2025. Most offences were related to malicious communications followed by harassment, and criminal damage to a building.
In 2025, there were 50 death threats reported - up from 31 the previous year.

title: I earn £120,000 a year making social media videos go viral
content_c:
I earn £120,000 a year making social media videos go viral
- Published
Eknoor Singh says he only needs his mobile phone and a decent internet connection to earn more than £120,000 a year.
The 22-year-old Londoner is a professional "clipper". He is paid by clients to make short, vertical videos for social media, in the hope of them going viral.
"The more views a clip gets, the more money I make," he says.
The way it typically works is that the client - who could be anyone from a clothing brand to a record label, movie studio, podcaster or influencer - has a longer video that the clipper watches first.
He or she then makes 30 to 60-second clips of what they consider to be the best bit or bits, and uploads them to Instagram, YouTube, TikTok or other platforms.
The idea is that the clippers, who are typically aged from 16 to 25, will have a better understanding of what will connect with that demographic, and get the short videos as many views as possible.
£10,000 a month
With clippers able to earn up to $3 (£2.30) per 1,000 views across platforms, it can be very lucrative if a particular clip does take off.
Singh says he got hooked on clipping last year when he made $300 from posting a short video of popstar Dua Lipa on Instagram.
"I was like, 'OK, this is a lot of money for simply posting a video.' I instantly knew how lucrative it could be."
Now he says he is earning "at least £10,000 a month".
He adds that he looks for clips that are funny, quick to watch and engaging, such as a short video he made in May of Sabrina Carpenter's reaction to having the tails of her dress stepped on at the Met Gala in New York. Singh did not reveal who the client was.
Many make nothing
For 24-year-old clipper Ethan Weems from Wichita, Kansas, it's a lucrative side hustle to his other video-making work. He says he makes "at least $1,000 a month" from clipping.
He does this by making short videos for YouTuber and podcaster Caleb Hammer, who is best known for hosting a show called Financial Audit, which analyses the personal finances of his guests.
Weems says clipping helps him make a living from home – giving him more time to spend with his wife and one-year-old son. "I don't want that typical nine-to-five job where I have to go into an office every day," he says.
Yet while some clippers can make good money, social media consultant Lia Haberman cautions that there are very few of them. "It mirrors the creator economy more broadly. The vast majority make little to nothing," she says.
Meanwhile, streaming industry analyst Devin Nash says it's easy to underestimate the time required to make clipping a success. He warns that successful clippers must "watch hours and hours of content, and they just live in that world".
Connecting clippers with their prospective clients are a number of intermediary websites, where available video jobs are listed.
These range from pages on general online forums such as Reddit and Discord, to dedicated clipping sites such as Clipping Culture, Vyro, Whop and Kick.
The latter websites take a fee from the companies wanting the work done. Clipping Culture lists clients including Capital Records, Universal Music Group and HBO Max.
For firms such as these, hiring a teenager or 20-something working from his or her bedroom is far cheaper than paying for traditional adverts on social media, and likely to be more effective in terms of getting eyeballs.
That's the experience of Boxabl, a Las Vegas-based firm that makes modular homes. "I think we've done probably a billion views [of clips] so far," says founder Galiano Tiramani, who features in many of the company's videos.
In the UK, Jimmy McLoughlin, a former Downing Street adviser and now host of the Jimmy's Jobs of the Future podcast, has also embraced clips.
"The clips are almost like trailers for the main events," he says. For instance, a recent podcast with Prime Minister Andy Burnham "had close to 50,000 long plays, but in terms of clips, it's done millions".
Evan Stanfield, the founder and boss of Clipping Culture, is himself just 21. He set up the business last year after dropping out of the University of Kansas.
Stanfield says that the website connects brands to more than 340,000 clippers from all over the world. He has a simple theory for the popularity of short videos: "People's attention spans are getting shorter and shorter."
He adds that making the clips is a young person's game because "they're most of the consumers of short-form videos".
Back in London, Eknoor Singh says he is "kind of clipping non-stop", wherever he is.
"I could be anywhere. I could go on holiday and make money."

  - Published15 September
description: Social media "clippers" make short, vertical videos that appear on the likes of Instagram and TikTok.

title: Argentina temporarily closes Iguazu Falls after El Niño-fuelled surge in water levels
content_c:
Heavy rainfall fuelled by a supersized El Niño weather pattern briefly forced Argentinian authorities to close tourist access to the famed Iguazu Falls, amid fears that rapidly rising water levels would cause the river to burst its banks.
National park officials took the precautionary measure on Monday when the Iguazu River’s flow exceeded 12,000 cubic metres per second – more than six times its average rate.
It later said the area would reopen to tourists on Tuesday, citing a “gradual decline” in the river’s flow.
José María Hervás, the director of the Iguazu national park, said access was closed because “it just keeps raining” and the volume of water being released from dams upstream on the Iguazu River was not falling, reported the Buenos Aires Times.
The Iguazu Falls, recognised by Unesco as one of the world’s largest and most impressive waterfalls, sits on the border of Argenina and Brazil and spans approximately 2,700 metres.
In 2023 and 2024, Argentinian officials closed the park on its side of the border over flooding caused by a previous El Niño cycle.
Meteorologists say the 2026-2027 El Niño, which causes global changes in winds and rainfall as well as erratic weather conditions, is certain to be the biggest ever recorded. Scientists now also think human-caused global heating is making El Niño’s more intense.
El Niño begins in the equatorial Pacific where changes in winds allow huge amounts of heat to escape the oceans and heat the atmosphere. It grows in the northern hemisphere autumn and peaks in December but has impacts well into the following year.
Last month, Argentina’s coastal region experienced above-average rainfall “similar to that seen during strong El Niño events,” the national meteorological service said.
