title: Яке 13 жовтня свято — все про цей день, яке церковне свято
content_c:
Яке 13 жовтня свято — все про цей день, яке церковне свято
13 жовтня, Міжнародний день зменшення небезпеки лих. Віряни вшановують пам’ять мучеників Карпа, Папіли й Агатоніки. До Нового року залишилося 84 дні.
13 жовтня 2026 року — вівторок. 1692-й день війни в Україні.
Яке свято 13 жовтня
13 жовтня віряни святкують День пам’яті мучеників Карпа, Папіли й Агатоніки. Карп був єпископом, а Папіла — дияконом. За переказами, їх заарештували через відмову приносити жертви язичницьким богам. Після катувань вони не зреклися християнської віри й були страчені. Агатоніка була християнкою, яка стала свідком їхніх страждань. Вона відкрито сповідувала свою віру і також прийняла мученицьку смерть.
13 жовтня в Україні і світі святкують День без бюстгальтера. Цього дня день жінок заохочують за бажанням відмовитися від бюстгальтера як символу свободи, прийняття власного тіла та привернення уваги до теми здоров’я грудей. Ініціатива набула популярності в соцмережах на початку 2010-х років і згодом стала асоціюватися з місяцем обізнаності про рак молочної залози, який проходить у жовтні. Водночас День без бюстгальтера не є офіційною медичною кампанією, а відмова від бюстгальтера не запобігає раку молочної залози.
Також 13 жовтня Міжнародний день костюма. Популярність свята пов’язують із серіалом «Як я зустрів вашу маму» (How I Met Your Mother) та персонажем Барні Стінсоном, якого зіграв Ніл Патрік Гарріс. Барні відомий своєю любов’ю до класичних костюмів і знаменитим закликом «Suit up!». Шанувальники серіалу підхопили цю ідею, і приблизно від 2010 року Suit Up Day почав поширюватися через соцмережі.
А ще 13 жовтня Міжнародний день зменшення небезпеки лих. Його започаткувала Генеральна Асамблея ООН 1989 року, щоб привернути увагу до того, як держави й громади можуть зменшувати ризики та наслідки природних і техногенних катастроф. Йдеться не лише про реагування на землетруси, повені, пожежі, посухи чи шторми, а передусім про профілактику і підготовку: системи раннього попередження, безпечне будівництво, плани евакуації, навчання населення та захист критичної інфраструктури.
13 жовтня святкують Міжнародний день простої мови. Він присвячений ідеї, що офіційні, юридичні, медичні, ділові та інші важливі тексти мають бути написані зрозумілою для звичайної людини мовою, без зайвої канцелярщини та складних конструкцій.
Також 13 жовтня День поширення інформації про метастатичний рак молочної залози. Він покликаний привернути увагу до людей, які живуть із метастатичним, або IV стадії, раком молочної залози. Метастатичним називають рак молочної залози, який поширився за межі грудей і прилеглих лімфатичних вузлів на інші органи чи частини тіла — наприклад, кістки, легені, печінку або мозок. Це не окремий вид раку: навіть після поширення пухлинні клітини зберігають характеристики раку молочної залози.
А ще 13 жовтня Всесвітній день боротьби з тромбозом. Його започаткувало 2014 року Міжнародне товариство з тромбозу і гемостазу (ISTH), щоб підвищувати обізнаність про тромбоз, його ознаки, фактори ризику та способи профілактики. Тромбоз виникає, коли в кровоносній судині утворюється згусток крові — тромб, який може частково або повністю перекрити кровотік. Особливу небезпеку становить венозна тромбоемболія, до якої належать тромбоз глибоких вен і тромбоемболія легеневої артерії.

title: Досрочный выход на пенсию для УБД: сколько лет стажа требуется
content_c:
Украинцы продолжают получать пенсии и другие социальные выплаты. Некоторые граждане могут досрочно выйти на пенсию при определенных условиях. В частности, таким правом обладают участники боевых действий (УБД). В Главном управлении Пенсионного фонда Украины (ПФУ) в Винницкой области рассказали, сколько лет страхового стажа необходимо иметь УБД, чтобы выйти на пенсию досрочно.
Когда УБД может выйти на пенсию
В ПФУ пояснили, что на назначение досрочной пенсии участники боевых действий имеют право после достижения мужчинами 55 лет, женщинами — 50 лет и при наличии страхового стажа не менее 25 лет у мужчин и не менее 20 лет у женщин. Соответствующая норма определена законом «Об общеобязательном государственном пенсионном страховании».
Так, к УБД относятся:
- военнослужащие, лица начальствующего и рядового состава органов внутренних дел, полицейские, принимавшие участие в боевых действиях;
- лица, которым присвоен статус участника боевых действий в соответствии с пунктами 20 и 21 статьи 6 закона «О статусе ветеранов войны, гарантиях их социальной защиты» (члены добровольческих формирований);
- лица из числа резервистов, военнообязанных и лиц, входивших в состав добровольческого формирования территориальной общины, которым присвоен статус УБД в соответствии с пунктом 19 статьи 6 (участники АТО).
Могут ли УБД назначить пенсию по возрасту
В Фонде добавили, что возможность назначения пенсии по возрасту целесообразна в случае, если УБД не приобрел право на пенсию за выслугу лет, предусмотренной законом «О пенсионном обеспечении лиц, уволенных с военной службы, и некоторых других лиц», либо если военнослужащий продолжает военную службу, но достиг вышеуказанного пенсионного возраста и приобрел необходимую продолжительность страхового стажа. То есть досрочная пенсия по возрасту назначается независимо от того, работает ли или проходит службу данное лицо.
«Лица, работавшие в воинских частях (вольнонаемные лица), принимавшие участие в боевых действиях и которым присвоен статус участника боевых действий, имеют все льготы, предусмотренные для данной категории ветеранов войны, кроме досрочного выхода на пенсию по возрасту», — говорится в сообщении.
В ПФУ подчеркнули, что законодательством предусмотрен досрочный выход на пенсию по возрасту и для членов семей погибших участников боевых действий: родителей, жен, мужей.
Недавно президент Украины подписал Закон № 4851-IX «О внесении изменений в Закон Украины «Об общеобязательном государственном пенсионном страховании» относительно подтверждения страхового стажа», который изменяет правила подтверждения страхового стажа и порядок назначения пенсий. Документ был принят Верховной Радой Украины на основе законопроекта № 13705-д и касается практически всех граждан, которые работали или работают официально. Подробнее об этом — в статье экономиста Елены Косенко «Новый закон о подтверждении стажа: что изменится для украинцев» на ZN.UA.

title: У Харкові через ворожу атаку постраждали 11 людей, зруйновано під'їзд чотириповерхівки – ДСНС
content_c:
Унаслідок масованого ворожого удару по Харкову ввечері 12 жовтня постраждали 11 людей, зокрема рятувальник, трьох осіб вдалося врятувати, повідомляє Державна служба з надзвичайних ситуацій.
"Під ударом опинилися житлові квартали та об'єкти цивільної інфраструктури в Холодногірському та Шевченківському районах міста. Одна з ракет влучила в чотириповерховий житловий будинок, унаслідок чого повністю зруйновано під'їзд. Під завалами можуть перебувати люди", – ідеться в повідомленні відомства.
У ДСНС зазначили, що під час ліквідації наслідків удару постраждав рятувальник, його госпіталізовано. На інших локаціях також зафіксовано пожежі та руйнування; гасіння вогню й аварійно-рятувальні роботи тривають.

title: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
content_c:
Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
- Published
Saudi Arabia's energy minister has vowed a "serious" response to the deadly attacks on the kingdom's airports and oil and gas facilities by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement.
"The events of recent weeks are serious. Our response must be equally serious," Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman told the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh.
On Sunday, a Pakistani man was killed in an attack on a terminal at the capital's King Khalid International Airport, Saudi authorities said. It came a day after a Houthi missile hit another terminal, killing 13 people and forcing its closure.
The Houthis said they launched the attacks in retaliation for "brutal Saudi aggression" against areas they control in western Yemen.
A Saudi-led coalition is providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces battling the Houthis on Yemen's Red Sea coast and other areas.
Explosions were heard again in Riyadh on Monday night, with the Saudi-led military coalition saying a ballistic missile had been intercepted and destroyed.
A Houthi spokesperson said the group had again targeted the airport.
Meanwhile, Qatar Airways has said it will temporarily suspend flights to Riyadh and the north-eastern city of Dammam.
Etihad Airways said it had cancelled flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam due to "regional disruption".
King Khalid airport is expected to remain closed until Saturday.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said early on Tuesday that the Houthis had shot down what he described as a Saudi "reconnaissance drone".
Meanwhile, the official spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed "two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards Khamis Mushait", in a statement shared on Tuesday.
The WPC Energy Congress opened on Sunday at a convention centre about 10km (6 miles) from Riyadh's airport, which has been attacked four times over the past week.
Last Thursday, three Saudis, including a pilot for the national airline Saudia, were killed in two strikes on an airport facility and an aircraft on the ground.
Another four Saudis, as well as two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian, one Sudanese and one Indian, were killed in Saturday's missile strike on Terminal 3.
On Sunday, a Pakistani resident was killed when a projectile hit Terminal 4, according to the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA).
King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was also attacked on Sunday evening, it said, but no casualties were reported.
Later, the Saudi-led coalition said its forces had intercepted a drone in Eastern Province and a missile launched by the Houthis towards the south-western city of Khamis Mushait.
Meanwhile, the Houthi-run health ministry said a child was killed and six other people were injured in a Saudi air strike on a home in the capital, Sanaa, on Sunday.
In his inaugural address to the WPC Energy Congress on Monday, Prince Abdul Aziz thanked industry executives and policymakers for attending despite the attacks.
"You know this country is safe and that we hold your protection at whole heart," he said.
But he also acknowledged that "energy security cannot be taken for granted" and that recent developments had "tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience".
Prince Abdul Aziz promised that his country would overcome those challenges.
"We, as Saudis, are fearless, combatant and determined people," he said. "We shall prove it to the world that whatever we are going through we will overcome it."
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.
On Sunday evening, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said in a video statement that its forces had launched missiles and drones at Riyadh and Dammam's airports, as well as two oil and gas facilities in Eastern Province, in response to 124 Saudi air strikes in Yemen over the previous 24 hours.
Sarea also reiterated a warning to airlines and passengers against using Saudi airports and airspace, except for journeys to and from the Islamic holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
The Houthis' forces, he vowed, would "continue their escalating operations deep inside Saudi, imposing the equation of 'a blockade for a blockade' and 'an escalation for an escalation' and targeting Saudi enemy reinforcements until the aggression ceases and the siege on our dear people is lifted".
Saturday's attack on Riyadh airport drew widespread international condemnation.
UN Secretary General António Guterres said he was "deeply shocked" and warned that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure were a violation of international law.
President Donald Trump said he would "make a decision" about the US joining Saudi Arabia's strikes on the Houthis. The US military is reportedly already providing intelligence and targeting support to the Saudi-led coalition.
Iran, which has repeatedly denied allegations that it provides weapons and training to the Houthis, said it was "deeply concerned" by the escalation and called for "dialogue and engagement" to resolve the situation.
Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.
A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The Yemeni government claimed it was behind that strike, saying it was trying to prevent an unauthorised Iranian plane from landing.
Last month, the Houthis launched a surprise offensive along Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and ousted pro-government forces from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea.
They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.
However, the seizure of the strait contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports after the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.
Last week, the Yemeni government announced the start of a new offensive aimed at retaking all territory held by the Houthis.
Pro-government forces said they were quickly able to retake areas around Bab al-Mandab with the help of intense Saudi air strikes, but the Houthis denied losing any territory.
  - Published24 September

title: Campaigners claim minister attempting to undermine 'Holiday Hunger Bill'
content_c:
Campaigners claim minister attempting to undermine 'Holiday Hunger Bill'
- Published
Campaigners have accused the education minister of attempting to undermine a proposed Stormont law which would help poorer families with the cost of food.
The Democratic Unionist Party's (DUP) Paul Givan has been consistently critical of the legislation which is being brought forward by Sinn Féin assembly member Danny Baker.
Givan has warned it would immediately cost his department £20m a year at a time when it is already struggling to balance its budget.
The Holiday Meals Payment Bill, external would create a new payment for families whose children receive free school meals which would be made during school holidays to help with the cost of food.
'Reservations'
The matter is due to be discussed in the assembly on Monday.
Givan has now proposed amendments which would give him the power to delay implementation.
He will need support from other parties for the amendments to be accepted.
It is not clear if he will get that support, although the Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) has expressed reservations about the proposal.
As it is based on school meals, the cost of the scheme would be on the Department of Education.
It is modelled on the School Holiday Food Grant scheme introduced during the pandemic, which paid qualifying families £27 per child every fortnight.
In April, Givan warned MLAs that his department did not have funding for the scheme, so they would be voting to cut education spending if they supported it.
He has now proposed amendments which would give him discretion to decide when the payments would take effect.
A coalition of campaign groups, including the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children (NSPCC) and Save the Children, say the amendments would mean "no guarantees about when, if ever, payments might begin".
They added: "We are calling on all political parties and all MLAs to reject the amendments tabled by the education minister and support the bill as it currently stands."
Baker has said the education minister is attempting to "obstruct" the implementation of the bill.
"His proposals would give him control over when, if ever, holiday hunger payments begin.
"This is an attempt to delay and undermine legislation that has the support of the majority of parties in the assembly."
A Department of Education spokesperson said the minister's amendments "do not seek to delay or block the Bill".
"They reflect the Department's duty to manage its budget responsibly, taking account of financial pressures, competing priorities and the impact of new spending on existing services, particularly at a time when education faces significant financial challenges across the system," they added.
"The amendments fulfil that duty while preserving the Bill's intended purpose. The Bill's key provisions remain unchanged, including eligibility, payment levels, holiday coverage and the Education Authority's responsibilities."
  - Published30 March 2023

title: Bullet hole in door and DNA evidence scrutinised in Beau Lamarre-Condon double murder trial
content_c:
A bullet hole left in a bedroom door and DNA found in the barrel of the firearm have been scrutinised in court as Beau Lamarre-Condon’s double murder trial continues in Sydney.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
The prosecution argues the policeman disguised himself as an UberEats rider before entering Baird’s home, shooting him twice – in the base of the neck and the right temple – and then shooting Davies through the bedroom door.
But the defence alleges they were killed in two separate incidents when Lamarre-Condon was acting in “self-defence”. During the tussle with Baird, the firearm was flung across the room where it was picked up by Davies, who later shot himself in a struggle with the policeman, the defence argues.
Defence lawyer John Stratton SC cross-examined crime scene officer Greg Moon on Tuesday, questioning the prosecution’s version of events.
Stratton pointed to a swab taken from the barrel of the alleged murder weapon, which returned a DNA profile that partially matched Davies. He then noted the hole in the bedroom door, through which the prosecution alleges Davies was shot, tested negative for blood.
Stratton suggested: “The possibility or likelihood of biological material finding its way from a wound of the deceased through a hole in the door less than a centimetre in width and into the barrel of a gun … approaches zero.”
But Moon told the New South Wales supreme court he disagreed.
“I believe it can still happen,” he said.
The defence does not dispute the couple were shot.
A diagram from Dr Kendall Bailey, who conducted the postmortem examinations of both men, suggested a bullet entered Baird’s body at the base of his neck and exited just below his lip.
Asked by crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC about the effect of this wound, Bailey told the jury it did not pass through any major vessels of the neck or the vertebral column or windpipe.
But that did not mean it was insignificant, the court heard.
“It still would be a very nasty injury and that fracturing of the jaw is a very nasty injury,” she told the court.
While it is potentially survivable, those kinds of injuries can be painful and cause some to pass out, though others may not lose consciousness, Bailey explained.
Hatfield then asked if a person with those injuries could speak.
The bullet went through the jaw and the base of the tongue, Bailey said, adding: “I don’t think anyone with that injury would be making any meaningful vocalisations.
“They could make a noise but that would be nothing that would be coherent,” she said.
Stratton questioned whether the exit and entry points of the bullet were clear. Bailey noted decompositional changes made it difficult to determine the direction in which the bullet had travelled, but said there were more features supporting trajectory from the back to the front than vice versa.
Bailey also explained the shot that entered the temple would go through the brain, where it would incapacitate a person.
Asked if that person would then be able to fling a gun to the other side of the room, she said the body could make some involuntary movements but “I don’t think that person is making any conscious movements”.
CT scans of Baird and Davies’ skulls showing the damage caused by the bullets were presented to the jury on Thursday.
Forensic radiologist Dr James Raleigh explained to the court there was a hole in the right side of Baird’s head at the temple region and multiple small bone fragments “presumably from that damage were run in a line across the inside of the skull”.
Davies’ wound was located in his face just above the left eyebrow, which Raleigh agreed was consistent with a bullet hole.
Two wounds on Davies’ thigh were consistent with a “single-bladed weapon”, Bailey said.
But she agreed those injuries likely took place after or at the time of death.
NSW police firearms examiner, Lucas Van Der Walt, showed the jury a model bullet cartridge and prop gun to demonstrate how Lamarre-Condon’s weapon would have been reloaded and racked, and the way a shell would be ejected.
When visiting the crime scene, he determined a bullet hole found in the floor must have been shot close to a vertical angle and said he had found the bullet in the subfloor of the terrace house.
He noted forensics teams didn’t always find bullets as they are small and travel at a velocity of 350 metres per second.
“Unless they reveal themselves in the open, you’re not going to get them,” he said.
The crime scene had also been cleaned extensively after the shootings, and there was a chance the bullet could have been removed, the court heard.
The jury is set to view Baird’s home in the coming days.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

title: Starlink India launch: Why Elon Musk is still waiting
content_c:
Starlink India launch: Why Elon Musk is still waiting
October 13, 2026
Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX, has escalated his criticism of the delay in launching Starlink in India. Last week, he sarcastically referred to Mukesh Ambani, one of India's richest people and chairman of Reliance Industries, as "Prime Minister Ambani" and accused his supporters of protecting a monopoly.
"Would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" Musk wrote on X, arguing that the service could bring internet access to underserved communities across India.
Rahul Gandhi, a leader of the opposition Indian National Congress, joined the discussion, writing: "Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy." Musk replied: "Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling."
A delayed launch and a war of words
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused Gandhi of championing Musk's interests, while party leaders defended the government's handling of the issue.
Speaking during the India Mobile Congress 2026 in New Delhi last week, Reliance Jio chairman Akash Ambani declined to comment on Musk's remarks. He said: "I have no comments to make. We want to keep our heads down and deliver value to our Indian consumers."
Akash, Mukesh Ambani's eldest son, also noted that Jio was progressing on its own end-to-end indigenous satellite broadband technology stack.
Meanwhile, Starlink — despite securing key approvals and signing distribution agreements with Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel — has yet to begin commercial operations in India.
Its low-earth-orbit satellites could provide internet access in remote villages, hilly regions and border areas where fiber-optic networks and mobile towers are expensive to build.
But the service would enter a market where mobile data is inexpensive and established telecom operators have extensive networks.
India's Ministry of Communications says security assessments for all three licensed satellite operators are under way and that they are at broadly the same regulatory stage.
In a statement, the ministry said every licensee must meet security conditions intended to protect users and their data. Once an assessment is completed, an operator can seek spectrum assignment. It described allegations that the framework was unfair or discriminatory as "baseless and misconceived."
Legitimate security concerns?
Starlink secured a satellite communications licence from the Department of Telecommunications and authorization from the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center in 2025. These approvals do not automatically permit commercial operations, however.
The security debate surrounding Starlink has intensified following remarks by BJP leader Nishikant Dubey, who chairs a parliamentary committee. In a post on X on October 11, Dubey said the panel had examined Starlink's security challenges.
"As the chairman of the parliamentary committee, our committee has understood the challenges facing the country's security agencies through Starlink," he wrote in Hindi.
Responding to Musk's criticism, Dubey added, "India is a healthy democratic, sovereign nation, and it does not change its security policy under pressure from social media or external figures."
Dubey did not specify the security risks or regulatory requirements holding up the launch.
Former intelligence officer and national security expert Yashovardhan Jha Azad said the impasse reflected commercial competition, regulatory uncertainty and legitimate security concerns.
"The central question is: who retains effective control over an essential communications service during a crisis?" Azad told DW.
He said India needed safeguards covering traffic routing, lawful interception under due process and cybersecurity.
"The existence of security requirements, however, does not establish why Starlink's application remains pending," Azad said. He pointed out that the government has not publicly detailed which specific conditions, if any, the company still needs to satisfy.
Investment, manufacturing and affordability
The delay in Starlink's launch has raised questions about the predictability of India's investment environment.
Economist Lekha Chakrabarty, who has studied the issue closely, said the problem was not that India was shutting its doors to foreign investment, but that companies could not plan around an open-ended approval process.
"The Starlink impasse is best read not as India closing its door to foreign investment, but as a failure to make an already open door predictably passable," Chakrabarty told DW.
She said security reviews were necessary given the sensitivity of satellite communications, which involve critical infrastructure, cross-border data, gateway control and lawful interception.
But the problem, she said, was the lack of transparency around approval criteria and timelines.
"Investors can price known rules, they cannot efficiently price discretionary, multi-agency processes with uncertain endpoints," Chakrabarty added.
Pankaj Mohindroo, chairman of the India Cellular and Electronics Association, said Starlink's entry could create opportunities for Indian electronics manufacturers in satellite terminals, antennas, communication modules and network equipment.
"India already has a strong trusted electronics manufacturing base, which provides an opportunity for global technology companies to develop local partnerships and strengthen domestic supply chains," he told DW.
Edited by: Srinivas Mazumdaru
description: Despite securing key approvals, the Starlink satellite internet service remains in regulatory limbo, raising questions about security clearances, competition and India’s investment climate.

Starlink India launch: Why Elon Musk is still waiting
October 13, 2026
Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX, has escalated his criticism of the delay in launching Starlink in India. Last week, he sarcastically referred to Mukesh Ambani, one of India's richest people and chairman of Reliance Industries, as "Prime Minister Ambani" and accused his supporters of protecting a monopoly.
"Would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" Musk wrote on X, arguing that the service could bring internet access to underserved communities across India.
Rahul Gandhi, a leader of the opposition Indian National Congress, joined the discussion, writing: "Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy." Musk replied: "Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling."
A delayed launch and a war of words
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused Gandhi of championing Musk's interests, while party leaders defended the government's handling of the issue.
Speaking during the India Mobile Congress 2026 in New Delhi last week, Reliance Jio chairman Akash Ambani declined to comment on Musk's remarks. He said: "I have no comments to make. We want to keep our heads down and deliver value to our Indian consumers."
Akash, Mukesh Ambani's eldest son, also noted that Jio was progressing on its own end-to-end indigenous satellite broadband technology stack.
Meanwhile, Starlink — despite securing key approvals and signing distribution agreements with Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel — has yet to begin commercial operations in India.
Its low-earth-orbit satellites could provide internet access in remote villages, hilly regions and border areas where fiber-optic networks and mobile towers are expensive to build.
But the service would enter a market where mobile data is inexpensive and established telecom operators have extensive networks.
India's Ministry of Communications says security assessments for all three licensed satellite operators are under way and that they are at broadly the same regulatory stage.
In a statement, the ministry said every licensee must meet security conditions intended to protect users and their data. Once an assessment is completed, an operator can seek spectrum assignment. It described allegations that the framework was unfair or discriminatory as "baseless and misconceived."

title: Papst für Lungenoperation im Krankenhaus
content_c:
Gemelli-Klinik Papst für Lungenoperation im Krankenhaus
Nach dem Fund eines Knotens in der Lunge will sich Papst Leo operieren lassen. Spätestens am Mittwoch soll der Eingriff durchgeführt werden.
Der Vatikan bemüht sich, Gelassenheit und Routine zu vermitteln. Papst Leo der Vierzehnte habe bislang auch in dieser Woche alle geplanten Termine wahrgenommen, hieß es. Nur bei einer Messe am Mittwoch wird er sich vertreten lassen: Die Predigt zum Abschluss des Bischofstreffens zu Ehe und Familie wird jetzt Kardinaldekan Luis Tagle halten. Er wurde erst vergangene Woche zum ranghöchsten Kardinal ernannt.
Am Dienstagvormittag wird der Papst in der Gemelli-Klinik aufgenommen. Dort steht ein eigener Trakt für ihn und seine engen Mitarbeiter bereit. Noch am Nachmittag oder am Mittwoch soll dann die Operation erfolgen.
Reisen ab Ende Oktober sollen wie geplant stattfinden
Der Papst hatte am Sonntag beim Angelus-Gebet auf dem Petersplatz erklärt, er werde sich einem Eingriff unterziehen. Die Ärzte hätten ihm zur Entfernung eines Knotens in der Lunge geraten. Dieser Knoten sei begrenzt und in einem frühen Stadium entdeckt worden. Im Vatikan ist von einem Zufallsfund bei einer Routineuntersuchung die Rede. Man rechnet nach der Operation mit etwa einer Woche Krankenhausaufenthalt.
An seinen Reiseplänen hält der Papst vorerst fest: Am 27.Oktober will er am Weltgebetstreffen in Assisi teilnehmen, am 6. November will er dann zu einer längeren Reise nach Südamerika aufbrechen - unter anderem nach Peru, wo er als Missionar und Bischof tätig war. Das hat auch ein argentinischer Erzbischof bestätigt, der den Papst gestern getroffen hat.

title: DFB-Frauen: Ena Mahmutovic nutzt ihre Chance im Tor und macht Druck auf Ann-Katrin Berger
content_c:
DFB-Frauen: Ena Mahmutovic nutzt Tor-Chance gegen Berger
12. Oktober 2026
Deutschland - Australien 4:2 (2:1)
Tore: 1:0 Kössler (23.), 2:0 Kössler (30.), 2:1 Kerr (45.+2), 3:1 Küver (83.), 3:2 McNamara (90.+3), 4:2 Nuesken (90.+4)
Zuschauer in Karlsruhe: 26.352
-----------------------
Mit Entschlossenheit, Tempo und vier schön herausgespielten Toren hat die deutsche Fußball-Nationalmannschaft der Frauen ihr Testspiel gegen Australien gewonnen und dabei nicht nur die Fans, sondern auch den Bundestrainer begeistert.
"Man sieht, wie die Mädels brennen, wie sie auch jetzt schon harmonieren, und dass wir unheimlich viel Qualität auf dem Platz und auch auf der Bank haben", freute sich Christian Wück nach dem verdienten 4:2-Erfolg seiner Mannschaft.
Da es einige prominente Ausfälle im deutschen Team gab - unter anderem Kapitänin Giulia Gwinn und Torjägerin Lea Schüller - mussten andere die Lücken füllen und taten das mit Bravour: Melissa Kössler empfahl sich mit ihren ersten beiden Länderspieltoren zur 2:0-Führung als Mittelstürmerin (23. und 30. Minute). Australiens Kapitänin Sam Kerr verkürzte kurz vor der Pause (45.+2).
In der Schlussphase traf dann Innenverteidigerin Camilla Küver per Kopfball zum 3:1 (83.), ehe Australiens Holly McNamara (90.+3) und Sjoeke Nüsken (90.+4) in der Nachspielzeit zum 4:2-Endstand trafen.
Ena Mahmutovic nutzt ihre Chance im Tor
Im Tor konnte mit Ena Mahmutovic eine Spielerin auf sich aufmerksam machen, die normalerweise auf der Ersatzbank sitzt. Nummer eins im deutschen Tor ist Ann-Katrin Berger, die sich nach dem Finale der UEFA Nations League im vergangenen Dezember nach kurzer Bedenkzeit entschied, mindestens für einen weiteren Turnierzyklus zur Verfügung zu stehen.
Allerdings fehlt die 35-Jährige diesmal in Absprache mit dem Trainerstab und auf eigenen Wunsch. Sie steht in den USA in der National Women's Soccer League für Tabellenführer Gotham FC im Tor und geht mit ihrem Klub in die heiße Phase der Saison. Bis Anfang November sind noch drei Partien zu absolvieren, danach beginnen die Playoffs.
Parallelen zu Bayern-Ersatzmann Jonas Urbig
So rückte bereits im Vorfeld der Testspiele gegen Australien und Japan (Dienstag, 17:45 Uhr MESZ) Mahmutovic in den Fokus. "Ena hat es verdient, dass sie das nächste Spiel macht", sagte Wück vergangene Woche. "Man darf nicht vergessen, dass sie in Slowenien [beim letzten WM-Qualifikationsspiel, Anm.d.Red.] schon die Null gehalten hat. Und ich hoffe, dass sie das wiederholen kann."
Die 22-jährige Torhüterin des FC Bayern München gilt als große Hoffnung im deutschen Tor und potentielle Nachfolgerin für Berger - ähnlich wie ihr Vereinskollege Jonas Urbig bei den Männern.
Beide sind 2003 geboren, beide stammen aus dem Bundesland Nordrhein-Westfalen, beiden wird im Verein wie im Nationalteam eine große Zukunft vorausgesagt. Einziger Unterschied: Anders als Urbig ist Mahmutovic im Klub bereits die Nummer eins. Vor der Saison 2025/2026 setzte sie sich im internen Duell gegen Maria Luisa Grohs durch und übernahm den Stammplatz zwischen den Pfosten.
Im DFB-Trikot muss sie dagegen noch warten - hier ist ihr wiederum Urbig einen Schritt voraus. Obwohl im Verein nur Nummer zwei, deutet nach den ersten vier Länderspielen unter demneuen Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp vieles darauf hin, dass Klopp Urbig im Vorfeld der Europameisterschaft 2028 zur neuen Nummer eins machen könnte.
Mahmutovic ist bei der anstehenden WM im kommenden Jahr eher als Ersatz eingeplant. Dennoch erhielt sie nun gegen Australien die nächste Chance und machte ihr drittes Länderspiel.
"Ich freu mich natürlich sehr", sagte sie vor dem Spiel. "Es ist natürlich immer was Besonderes, dann auch noch gegen eine Mannschaft von einem anderen Kontinent. Das ist glaube ich sehr hilfreich, wenn wir jetzt auch auf die WM blicken, uns mit denen zu messen."
Wück: "Berger einen Tacken voraus"
Ena sei "die Zukunft der Nationalmannschaft", schwärmte auch Bayern-Direktorin Bianca Rech kürzlich und machte sich dafür stark, dass ihre Keeperin nicht nur nominiert werde, sondern auch regelmäßig spielen dürfe. Berger sei, so Wück, aber "noch einen Tacken voraus".
Gleichzeitig lobte der Bundestrainer Mahmutovic: "Die Leistungen von Ena sind sehr gut. Sie hat mittlerweile auch eine gute Präsenz auf dem Platz", erklärte er und kündigte an: "Sie wird ihre Spielzeit bekommen."
Debüt mit Patzer, Debüt als Feldspielerin
Ihren Vertrag in München hat Mahmutovic Ende September bis 2029 verlängert. Sie kam zuvor aber nur auf zwei Einsätze in der A-Nationalmannschaft. Dabei war sie bereits im Februar 2023 zum ersten Mal für das Team nominiert. Ihr Debüt ist auch schon fast zwei Jahre her.
Im Dezember 2024 stand sie im Freundschaftsspiel gegen Italien auf dem Platz und patzte am Ende entscheidend. Nach einem Rückpass verlor sie den Ball an eine heraneilende Stürmerin, die ihr das Leder abnahm und locker zum 2:1-Siegtor ins leere Tor einschieben konnte. Danach kam bislang nur noch ein weiterer Länderspieleinsatz hinzu. Allerdings stand Mahmutovic im Kader der deutschen Mannschaft für die Europameisterschaft 2025.
Wäre es nach ihrem Vater gegangen, der aus Montenegro stammt, wäre Mahmutovic gar keine Torhüterin geworden. "Er sagt immer noch, ich wäre draußen besser gewesen, weil ich beide Füße gut einsetzen kann", sagt sie.
Dass muss wohl auch ihr damaliger Trainer Thomas Gerstner beim MSV Duisburg so gesehen haben, als er Mahmutovic im Mai 2020 ihr Bundesliga-Debüt bescherte. Allerdings sammelte die damals erst 16-Jährige nicht als Torhüterin erste Spielminuten.
Duisburg hatte zu viele Ausfälle und so musste die Ersatztorhüterin kurz vor dem Abpfiff als Feldspielerin einspringen: "In der Nachspielzeit hat mich der Trainer dann eingewechselt", erinnert sie sich. "Ich durfte zwei Sprints machen, so war eben mein Debüt."
Heute überwiegen dagegen Mahmutovics Vorzüge im Tor. "Sie ist eine der talentiertesten Torhüterinnen der Welt", schwärmte Bayern-Trainer José Barcala. Sie sei eine, die Spiele entscheiden könne, so der Spanier. Vielleicht ja in Zukunft auch regelmäßig im DFB-Team.
Der Artikel wurde am 9. und am 12. Oktober aktualisiert.
description: Die DFB-Frauen gewinnen ihr Testspiel gegen Australien. Im Tor macht Ena Mahmutovic dabei eine gute Figur. Die 22-jährige Bayern-Keeperin gilt als Nachfolgerin von Ann-Katrin Berger und kann Punkte sammeln.

Danach kam bislang nur noch ein weiterer Länderspieleinsatz hinzu. Allerdings stand Mahmutovic im Kader der deutschen Mannschaft für die Europameisterschaft 2025.
Wäre es nach ihrem Vater gegangen, der aus Montenegro stammt, wäre Mahmutovic gar keine Torhüterin geworden. "Er sagt immer noch, ich wäre draußen besser gewesen, weil ich beide Füße gut einsetzen kann", sagt sie.
Dass muss wohl auch ihr damaliger Trainer Thomas Gerstner beim MSV Duisburg so gesehen haben, als er Mahmutovic im Mai 2020 ihr Bundesliga-Debüt bescherte. Allerdings sammelte die damals erst 16-Jährige nicht als Torhüterin erste Spielminuten.
Duisburg hatte zu viele Ausfälle und so musste die Ersatztorhüterin kurz vor dem Abpfiff als Feldspielerin einspringen: "In der Nachspielzeit hat mich der Trainer dann eingewechselt", erinnert sie sich. "Ich durfte zwei Sprints machen, so war eben mein Debüt."
Heute überwiegen dagegen Mahmutovics Vorzüge im Tor. "Sie ist eine der talentiertesten Torhüterinnen der Welt", schwärmte Bayern-Trainer José Barcala. Sie sei eine, die Spiele entscheiden könne, so der Spanier. Vielleicht ja in Zukunft auch regelmäßig im DFB-Team.
Der Artikel wurde am 9. und am 12. Oktober aktualisiert.

title: “Угода” Трампа про припинення вогню розв'язала Путіну руки на зиму: ISW попередили про моторошний сценарій
content_c:
“Угода” Трампа про припинення вогню розв'язала Путіну руки на зиму: ISW попередили про моторошний сценарій
За аналізом ISW, ініціатива США забороняє Україні бити по вразливих російських НПЗ, але залишає Путіну повну свободу для нищення українських електростанцій узимку 2026–2027 років.
Заява президента США Дональда Трампа про так зване «енергетичне перемир’я» виявилася лише потенційною пропозицією, яка наразі грає виключно на користь Кремля. Станом на 12 жовтня жодних домовленостей між Україною та Росією немає, а сам формат ініціативи створює смертельну загрозу для української енергосистеми напередодні зими.
Про це повідомляє Інститут вивчення війни (ISW) у своєму свіжому звіті.
Удари по енергетиці не припиняються: РФ продовжує терор
За даними аналітиків ISW, Росія навіть не думала зупиняти обстріли. У ніч проти 12 жовтня окупанти завдали чергових комбінованих ударів по українських об’єктах:
- уражено теплоелектроцентраль (ТЕЦ) на захід від Харкова;
- пошкоджено інфраструктуру газовидобутку в Харківській області;
- завдано удару по нафтобазі в Сарнах на Рівненщині.
Президент України Володимир Зеленський заявив, що лише протягом 12 жовтня російські війська атакували шість об’єктів енергетики. При цьому українські Сили оборони у відповідь утримувалися від ударів по енергетичній інфраструктурі РФ.
Зеленський наголосив: Україна готова до повного «енергетичного перемир’я» і не битиме по російських об’єктах, якщо Москва піде на взаємні кроки та офіційно зафіксує угоду.
Пастка у формі «пропозиції»: що насправді задекларував Трамп
Джерело в Білому домі в коментарі виданню Axios підтвердило, що скандальна заява Дональда Трампа в мережі Truth Social від 11 жовтня стосувалася лише «потенційної угоди», а не реального припинення вогню. Жодна зі сторін домовленостей не підписувала.
Як з’ясувалося, пропозиція Трампа передбачає лише мораторій на удари по нафтопереробних заводах (НПЗ) з можливим розширенням на інші об’єкти в майбутньому.
В ISW наголошують: у нинішньому вигляді ця пропозиція є односторонньою поступкою на користь Росії:
- Нерівні умови: У Росії працюють десятки великих НПЗ, які є критичними для її економіки та воєнної машини. В України ж залишився лише один такий об’єкт.
- Карт-бланш на зимовий терор: «Угода» взагалі не захищає українські електричні станції. Це дозволить РФ безперешкодно продовжувати свою масовану ракетно-дронову кампанію проти української енергетики впродовж зими 2026–2027 років.
Таким чином, запропонований формат фактично зв’язує руки Україні, забороняючи бити по найвразливіших місцях агресора, але дає Путіну повну свободу дій для заморожування українських міст.
Що передувало
Нагадаємо, президент США домовився з Володимиром Путіним про великі постачання російського дизелю до США та інших країн.
За його словами, Росія має поставити понад 300 тисяч тонн дизелю одразу, ще 500 тисяч тонн — у листопаді, а згодом можливі додаткові партії.
Натомість у Сенаті США Трампа звинуватили в порушенні закону через російський дизель.
Потім Трамп знову висловився про скандальну угоду щодо пального з РФ і назвав своє рішення користю для народу США.
Тим часом ЗМІ повідомили, що США можуть залишити Україну без розвідданих, якщо Київ не припинить бомбити НПЗ Росії.

title: Зависимость Украины от США сохраняется в трех ключевых сферах — The Telegraph
content_c:
Президент США Дональд Трамп вновь выступил против президента Владимира Зеленского и в очередной раз продемонстрировал лояльность по отношению к российскому диктатору Владимиру Путину. В течение одного дня Трамп заявил, что Украине пора выбрать нового президента, и объявил о договоренности с Путиным об импорте российского дизельного топлива накануне выборов в Конгресс США.
Как пишет The Telegraph, эти действия напомнили первые месяцы президентства Трампа в 2025 году, когда он пытался договориться с Путиным, ослабить позиции Зеленского и заставить Украину согласиться на мирное соглашение на условиях России. И хотя сегодня у Вашингтона меньше рычагов влияния на Киев, Украина по-прежнему зависит от США в трех важных сферах.
Как пишут в издании, сегодня у Трампа действительно гораздо меньше возможностей оказывать давление на Зеленского, ведь США больше не выделяют новых значительных пакетов помощи Украине. В то же время американское оружие продолжает поступать в страну, но его закупки оплачивают европейские союзники Украины.
ЕС компенсировал Украине недостаток американской помощи после решения Трампа ее отменить, согласившись предоставить Киеву 90 млрд евро на этот и следующий годы. Благодаря этой поддержке Зеленский теперь значительно меньше зависит от Трампа, чем раньше.
Впрочем, первой из трех важных сфер зависимости остаётся разведывательная информация, необходимая украинским военным для проведения операций, в частности дальнобойных ударов по объектам в России.
По оценкам, среди американских государственных структур поддержку Украине продолжают оказывать Центральное разведывательное управление (ЦРУ) и другие разведывательные службы. В частности, они передают точные спутниковые данные, которые помогают украинским военным все точнее поражать цели на российской территории.
В прошлом году Трамп на короткое время прекратил передачу разведывательных данных Украине, пытаясь усилить давление на Зеленского. Из-за этого некоторые европейские страны начали искать способы компенсировать недостаток такой помощи. В январе президент Франции Эммануэль Макрон заявил, что ранее Украина в значительной степени зависела от американской разведки, однако теперь Франция обеспечивает не менее двух третей ее потребностей в этой сфере.
Независимые эксперты тем временем не согласились с оценкой Макрона, отметив, что ни одна европейская страна, в частности Франция, не обладает такими возможностями для сбора спутниковых разведданных, как США. В то же время, как отмечается в издании, Украина смогла хотя бы частично уменьшить свою зависимость от американской разведки, которая имеет решающее значение для её обороны.
Вторая и, вероятно, самая острая проблема — зависимость Украины от поставок ракет-перехватчиков для борьбы с баллистическими ракетами. На данный момент только американские системы Patriot способны сбивать самые мощные ракеты, которыми Россия ежедневно атакует украинские города.
Еще до того, как Трамп в последний раз раскритиковал Зеленского, у Украины закончились запасы важных ракет-перехватчиков PAC-3. Основной причиной стало то, что имеющиеся американские запасы этих ракет перебросили на Ближний Восток, чтобы справиться с последствиями войны США против Ирана, отмечают в издании.
В июле пять европейских оборонных компаний объединили усилия и начали совместный проект по созданию современной ракеты-перехватчика для уничтожения баллистических ракет. Украина также работает над разработкой собственного перехватчика в сотрудничестве с другими европейскими союзниками.
Один из этих проектов в будущем может помочь Украине перестать зависеть от США в вопросе защиты от баллистических ракет. Однако The Telegraph пишет, что создать первый образец, пригодный для испытаний, разработчики смогут не раньше следующего года.
Третьей сферой зависимости Украины остается закупка американского оружия за деньги европейских союзников в рамках программы НАТО под названием PURL. По имеющейся информации, американские чиновники уже предупредили европейских коллег, что Трамп может остановить поставки вооружения по этой программе, если Зеленский не прекратит украинские удары по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам.
Возможность Европы заменить американские поставки будет зависеть от того, сколько оружия способны производить европейские страны. В настоящее время их оборонные предприятия уже не успевают удовлетворять возросший спрос, который усилился из-за увеличения военных расходов, особенно в Германии и Польше.
В частности, европейским правительствам придётся определить, готовы ли они сократить поставки оружия собственным армиям, чтобы передать больше вооружения Украине. Однако в ближайшее время из-за высокого спроса на оружие Европа может оказаться не в состоянии полностью заменить американские поставки, если США их сократят.
В целом Зеленский сейчас меньше зависит от США, чем в начале, когда Трамп начал угрожать ему и критиковать его действия. В то же время европейские союзники Украины вряд ли смогут полностью заменить разведывательные данные о целях, которые предоставляют США. Что касается ракет-перехватчиков и других видов вооружения, определенные решения можно найти, однако на это потребуется время.
The Telegraph отмечает, что, несмотря на усилия Зеленского, направленные на уменьшение зависимости от Вашингтона, Трамп и дальше может оказывать давление на украинского президента, создавая дополнительные трудности для Украины.

Он также заявлял, что Украина готова прекратить эти удары, если Россия остановит атаки на украинскую энергетическую инфраструктуру.
Axios писало, что украинский чиновник также утверждал, что во время переговоров Стив Уиткофф и Джаред Кушнер угрожали прекратить передачу Украине американских разведывательных данных, если Киев продолжит игнорировать просьбы Трампа. Однако представитель США опроверг информацию о том, что американская сторона выдвигала такие угрозы.
О том, какие факторы определяют цену на дизельное топливо и при каких условиях энергетическое перемирие выгодно Украине, в статье ZN.UA «Трамп обвиняет Киев в дорогом дизеле. Кто на самом деле раскачивает рынок и что делать Украине» пишет директор энергетических и инфраструктурных программ Центра Разумкова Владимир Омельченко.
description: В то же время сегодня у Дональда Трампа гораздо меньше возможностей оказывать давление на Владимира Зеленского.
content:
Президент США Дональд Трамп вновь выступил против президента Владимира Зеленского и в очередной раз продемонстрировал лояльность по отношению к российскому диктатору Владимиру Путину. В течение одного дня Трамп заявил, что Украине пора выбрать нового президента, и объявил о договоренности с Путиным об импорте российского дизельного топлива накануне выборов в Конгресс США.
Как пишет The Telegraph, эти действия напомнили первые месяцы президентства Трампа в 2025 году, когда он пытался договориться с Путиным, ослабить позиции Зеленского и заставить Украину согласиться на мирное соглашение на условиях России. И хотя сегодня у Вашингтона меньше рычагов влияния на Киев, Украина по-прежнему зависит от США в трех важных сферах.
Как пишут в издании, сегодня у Трампа действительно гораздо меньше возможностей оказывать давление на Зеленского, ведь США больше не выделяют новых значительных пакетов помощи Украине. В то же время американское оружие продолжает поступать в страну, но его закупки оплачивают европейские союзники Украины.
ЕС компенсировал Украине недостаток американской помощи после решения Трампа ее отменить, согласившись предоставить Киеву 90 млрд евро на этот и следующий годы. Благодаря этой поддержке Зеленский теперь значительно меньше зависит от Трампа, чем раньше.
Впрочем, первой из трех важных сфер зависимости остаётся разведывательная информация, необходимая украинским военным для проведения операций, в частности дальнобойных ударов по объектам в России.

Независимые эксперты тем временем не согласились с оценкой Макрона, отметив, что ни одна европейская страна, в частности Франция, не обладает такими возможностями для сбора спутниковых разведданных, как США. В то же время, как отмечается в издании, Украина смогла хотя бы частично уменьшить свою зависимость от американской разведки, которая имеет решающее значение для её обороны.

title: Десятеро людей постраждали в Харкові внаслідок масованої атаки
content_c:
У понеділок ввечері ЗС РФ завдали масованого удару по Харкову, застосувавши, за попередніми даними, 9 малогабаритних крилатих ракет S-8000 "Бандероль", загалом постраждали 10 людей.
"Найбільших руйнувань зазнав п'ятиповерховий житловий будинок у Холодногірському районі міста. Внаслідок удару постраждали восьмеро людей, серед них – співробітник ДСНС... Також у Холодногірському районі внаслідок влучання на території приватного домоволодіння двоє людей зазнали гострої реакції на стрес", – повідомляє пресслужба Харківської облпрокуратури.
Окрім того, у Шевченківському районі Харкова пошкоджено багатоквартирні житлові будинки, автомобілі, магазини та приміщення банку.
На місцях влучань працюють усі профільні служби. Інформація щодо наслідків атаки уточнюється.
Розпочато досудові розслідування за фактами вчинення воєнних злочинів (ч. 1 ст. 438 КК України).

title: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
content_c:
Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
- Published
Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
Hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight, according to one supermarket chain affected.
The chief executive of Coopérative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack.
More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand were affected, with a spokesman saying that another 100 shops were urgently disconnected from the internet to prevent the same thing happening to them.
Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.
The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.
Normally, supermarket freezers go through a short period of defrosting overnight, in which temperatures rise slightly. But the hackers ordered the units to heat up and stay hot, although Danfoss did not confirm any reports about just how warm the fridges and freezers could become in that process.
Danfoss said the affected cold units were older models whose security software could not be updated to ward off a risk they had identified.
The firm added in a statement that it had "long advised" businesses to keep supported systems up to date.
"Reliable refrigeration is critical to our customers' operations, and we remain committed to supporting our customers and helping them maintain secure and reliable systems they are used to."
The full scale of the attack is unclear, but figures supplied by individual chains suggest about 400 stores were affected out of 15,000 or so overall in France.
Carrefour said fridges in 80 of its 6,000 stores were hacked, while Monoprix said 5% of its 400-plus stores had been hit, with food removed from sale if its condition could not be guaranteed.
In a statement to the BBC, Mousquetaires Group - which owns Intermarché and Netto - said some fresh and frozen food display units remained out of service on Monday afternoon.
The stores had "taken all necessary precautions to remove the products from these units", it said, adding that staff were working to restock the shelves "as soon as possible".
Intermarché said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported.
As a result of the attack, managers arriving at branches of several supermarket chains on Monday morning were hit by a wave of hot air from the freezers. In some places there were even small fires.
French broadcaster BFMTV published an image showing a freezer in an ice cream aisle displaying a temperature of 26.5C.
Two supermarkets in the Alsace region reported losses of €270,000 (£228,000) between them, the broadcaster added, meaning the nationwide total could run into the millions.
French prosecutors have opened a specific cyber-crime investigation into the incident, which the Paris prosecutor's office called a "large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France".
European Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen condemned the hack in a post on X and added: "Food security requires more attention at all levels. Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality."
In a post on X, Coopérative chief executive Dominique Schelcher said staff were "fully mobilised, in co-ordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible".
He called for an investigation into the hack and said targeting equipment essential to the French food supply was "unacceptable".

Carrefour said fridges in 80 of its 6,000 stores were hacked, while Monoprix said 5% of its 400-plus stores had been hit, with food removed from sale if its condition could not be guaranteed.
In a statement to the BBC, Mousquetaires Group - which owns Intermarché and Netto - said some fresh and frozen food display units remained out of service on Monday afternoon.
The stores had "taken all necessary precautions to remove the products from these units", it said, adding that staff were working to restock the shelves "as soon as possible".
Intermarché said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported.
As a result of the attack, managers arriving at branches of several supermarket chains on Monday morning were hit by a wave of hot air from the freezers. In some places there were even small fires.
French broadcaster BFMTV published an image showing a freezer in an ice cream aisle displaying a temperature of 26.5C.
Two supermarkets in the Alsace region reported losses of €270,000 (£228,000) between them, the broadcaster added, meaning the nationwide total could run into the millions.
French prosecutors have opened a specific cyber-crime investigation into the incident, which the Paris prosecutor's office called a "large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France".
European Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen condemned the hack in a post on X and added: "Food security requires more attention at all levels. Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality."
In a post on X, Coopérative chief executive Dominique Schelcher said staff were "fully mobilised, in co-ordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible".
He called for an investigation into the hack and said targeting equipment essential to the French food supply was "unacceptable".

title: Tuesday briefing: Could Burnham take Britain back towards the EU?
content_c:
Good morning. After a holiday spent contracting nursery bugs from an 11-month-old, it’s good to return. Yesterday, Andy Burnham marked his first day back after party conference by calling for a closer relationship with the EU and drawing a line under a decade of “drift and division”. On Sunday, he said it was “clear” the Kremlin had been involved with the 2016 Brexit referendum vote.
Both statements mark a break, rhetorically at least, from his predecessors. Conservative governments long insisted there was no evidence of Russian interference in the Brexit vote. Keir Starmer attempted to put the entire issue of Brexit behind him, treating it as a historic event rather than a cause of economic pain.
But for all his words about a closer relationship with the EU, Burnham has kept the details pretty vague. Today’s newsletter, with the help of the Guardian’s Brussels correspondent Jennifer Rankin and our senior political correspondent Peter Walker, asks what his stance might actually amount to. That’s after the headlines.
Five big stories
- 
  UK | Andy Burnham said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps were “almost certainly” behind threats to RAF Fairford, the firmest attribution of responsibility made so far by the UK after an incident late last month.
- 
  UK politics | A close adviser to Nigel Farage had an influential role at a national polling company despite not being publicly associated with the firm, the Guardian revealed.
- 
  Ukraine | Volodymyr Zelenskyy has vowed to respond to Russia’s continuing attacks on the Ukrainian power grid as European leaders rally around Kyiv amid a feud with Donald Trump over Ukraine’s strikes on oil refineries.
- 
  Israel | Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the country’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of soldiers and officers interviewed in the documentary NAZA and prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.
- 
  US news | RJ Mitte, the young actor best known for playing Walter White Jr in the award-winning TV series Breaking Bad, died on Monday. He was 34.
In depth: What does Burnham want from Europe?
In the years after it voted to leave the European Union, Britain became something of a laughing stock among EU member states. “It was like a box set TV drama. People in Brussels would be staying up to watch votes in the House of Commons,” Jennifer Rankin, who moved to Brussels to cover the EU for the Guardian in January 2016, tells me. Civil servants in Brussels grew to regard the UK as one might regard a belligerent and ungrateful elderly relative, an impression that reached its apotheosis when the former Northern Ireland secretary Brandon Lewis admitted that the UK’s Brexit arrangements for Northern Ireland would break international law (albeit in a “very specific and limited way”.)
“From 2016 to 2020, the UK was seen as a model of how not to run your country,” Jennifer says. This impression softened after the passing of the Withdrawal Agreement Act in early 2020, and the Windsor framework deal, which amended the arrangements under the Northern Ireland protocol in 2023. “That was a turning point in drawing a line under the bad blood of the Brexit years,” Jennifer says. Keir Starmer’s government then sought to cooperate with the EU on various issues such as security, food and fishing, but the “reset” he pledged to deliver was tightly circumscribed by his red lines: no rejoining the single market, no customs union, no freedom of movement.
After his conference speech, Burnham suggested he might be open to reconsidering this when he suggested, somewhat cryptically, that the UK could go “all the way” (presumably towards full EU membership), and yesterday he called for a “longer-term discussion” about Britain’s relationship with the EU. But what might that actually mean?
Could the UK rejoin the EU?
Burnham has been “showing a lot of ankle” to remainers over the last few weeks, Peter Walker tells me. During his Labour conference speech, he promised to lay out “different options” for Britain’s long-term relationship with Europe, and acknowledged that Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.
“It’s pretty clear that a decent majority of people would like to push a switch that meant Brexit had never happened,” Peter says. Indeed, a YouGov poll in January 2025 found that just 11% of people thought Brexit had been more of a success than a failure. And as recently as last week, the Messina Group, a polling company, reported that half of voters say they would like to rejoin the EU. The economic consequences of Brexit are now well known, and research has estimated that, a decade after the referendum, UK GDP per head is between 6% and 8% lower than it would have been without Brexit. Yet reversing this decision would require another referendum, which would be politically fraught, reigniting a debate that splintered the country a decade ago, and reducing a highly complex and technical issue to a binary decision.
It’s hard to imagine Burnham – or any politician, for that matter – wanting to fight the next election while pledging something so divisive. Notably, even the Liberal Democrats, the most pro-EU of the major parties, favour rejoining the single market and customs union but describe UK membership of the EU as a “long-term goal” rather than an immediate priority.
What other options are on the table?
If a second referendum seems like a vanishingly distant prospect, other changes could take place without one. In the combustive years after Brexit, there was a short-lived hope that the UK might pursue its own version of the Norway model, allowing it to become a member of the European Economic Area. “It was the Conservatives who decided to pursue the hardest Brexit possible,” Peter reminds me.
In theory, a softer deal could mean rejoining the single market and customs union. But this would mean breaking Labour’s red lines, which Burnham has said he will stick to. And if the UK was to rejoin the single market but remain outside the EU, it would be forced to accept rules that it had no power to shape. “As soon as you look at the democratic deficit that comes with single market membership, the case for rejoining the EU becomes stronger,” Jennifer tells me.
The debate over rejoining the EU is often conducted in relatively parochial terms, as if it only concerns Britain. But the UK’s future relationship with the EU will be largely shaped by the member states of a union that has changed significantly since the referendum. Far-right parties are gaining power in France and Germany, while the mercantilist politics of China and the US have inspired the EU’s Made in Europe agenda, a series of protectionist laws designed to bolster European industry and reduce reliance on Chinese imports.
In this context, Burnham may decide it’s better to be inside the tent than outside it. The Made in Europe agenda is particularly concerning for the government, since UK industry could suffer if exports were legally classified as “non-European” goods under these new laws. But as Mujtaba Rahman wrote in an interesting opinion piece for the Guardian in July, “any serious rejoin debate must start from an honest assessment of what the EU has become”.
What happens next?
Right now, the longer term outcome is anyone’s guess. In his statement to the Commons, Burnham confirmed that the planned UK-EU summit will go ahead in November. Negotiators are expected to discuss a trade deal on food and drink, a deal on emissions trading, a plan to link the energy systems of the EU and UK and the new youth mobility scheme. These areas were all discussed at last years’ UK-EU talks, so Burnham wasn’t announcing anything we didn’t already know.
“There’s a lot of frustration in Brussels that the UK has been talking a big game on a reset with the EU, without actually changing very much,” Jennifer says. “The theme over the last ten years is that the EU has always been waiting for the UK to define what it wants. The rhetoric may be warmer, but the substance has stayed the same.”
What else we’ve been enjoying
- 
  I have always found that TV – with its twisting plotlines, and lack of demands – is a good cure for grief. Today’s one change that worked, by writer Georgina Elliott, on how the cinema gave her some focus after the death of her brother, poignantly depicted what it’s like to muddle through such times. Poppy Noor, newsletters team
- 
  Chloe Kerleroux’s photo essay about Atlanta’s Bill Pickett rodeo is a beautiful window into a competition which encompasses athleticism, hip-hop, fashion and the celebration of contemporary Black cowboy and cowgirl culture. Lucinda Everett, newsletters team
- 
  Here’s a line I didn’t expect to read today: professor Devi Sridhar, chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh, is worried about the pneumonic plague (although it might not be for the reasons you suspect). Poppy
- 
  Kiran Sidhu was touching, on considering who to pass her most prized possessions down to in her will since she doesn’t have children. Poppy
- 
  I, too, have been had by the myth that my (small amount of) muscle will turn into fat if I don’t force myself into a few push-ups every week. Not so, according to this week’s Is it true that … column – although what does happen when you stop exercising isn’t that much more reassuring. Poppy
Sport

Football | Almost half of female footballers are considering leaving the sport because of financial concerns or psychological stress, and 57% have struggled with their mental health, according to a report highlighting the working conditions for players worldwide.
Sport | Manchester United have endured their worst league start in 40 years but coach Michael Carrick insists he does not feel under pressure and has said his captain, Bruno Fernandes, will rediscover his form.
The front pages
The Guardian leads with “PM: Britain’s relationship with EU ‘not good enough’”. The i has “Burnham ready to sign new EU deal next month – as he attacks Brexit ‘damage’”. The Mail says “Burnham in retreat over Russia Brexit ‘lies’”.
The Times splashes on “Cut screen time in class ‘for sake of pupil health’”. The Financial Times has “Putin breaking ‘ceasefire’ on energy targets, says Zelenskyy”. The Mirror reports on comments from Reform’s Robert Jenrick on migrants, under the headline “Horrifying”.
Today in Focus: The Latest
Trump rewards Putin and betrays Ukraine with Russia diesel deal
Donald Trump’s deal to buy Russian diesel has been met with fury from Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said it was ‘a weak decision’ and would generate ‘billions’ in extra revenue for Putin’s war effort. The Ukrainian president has also rejected US calls for an ‘energy ceasefire’, which would require Kyiv to stop striking oil refineries, saying Moscow must first end its attacks on energy infrastructure. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s senior international correspondent, Luke Harding.
Cartoon of the day | Ben Jennings
The Upside
A bit of good news to remind you that the world’s not all bad
The Naffah family has been making church bells in the Lebanese town of Beit Chabab for three centuries. Led by master bell-maker Naffah Naffah and his two sons, their workshop is the last remaining production centre for church bells in Lebanon and the only source of church bells for much of the Middle East.
Crafted using a mix of modern and ancient tools, each bell takes about two months to make and bears the names of those who worked on it. Naffah and his sons Charbel and Youssef are determined to preserve the tradition. Charbel will succeed his father as master of the workshop and Youssef helps alongside studying medicine, but says he would take Charbel’s place if needed.
“Traditions are important to us,” he says. “We are living and breathing tradition here in this workshop.”

title: Can South Korea and Ukraine resolve their diplomatic spat over North Korean POWs?
content_c:
Can South Korea and Ukraine resolve their diplomatic spat?
October 12, 2026
South Korea's ambassador to Kyiv returned to Seoul on Saturday, his recall the latest in a series of tit-for-tat actions that have severely strained bilateral ties.
The sudden deterioration in their relationship can be traced back to September 23, when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the United Nations General Assembly in New York that Ukraine had transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea.
The soldiers had been captured by Ukrainian forces in the Russian Kursk region in January 2025 as they fought alongside Russian troops.
The South Korean government immediately expressed its anger at Zelenskyy's revelation, insisting that the two governments had reached an agreement to keep the transfer of the two men in mid-September a secret.
Kyiv hit back, by saying that no confidentiality agreement had been in place, to which South Korea accused Ukraine of effectively lying and demanded an official explanation and an apology.
Ukraine has attempted to smooth over what it has called a "diplomatic understanding," but stopped short of the public apology that was expected in Seoul.
Then, reports emerged last week that a close adviser to Zelenskyy had said that more than 176,000 tons of diesel and other energy products were shipped to Russia from South Korean ports in July and August of this year, which would be a breach of international sanctions.
The office of president Lee Jae Myung in Seoul denied the accusation, and two days later recalled its ambassador to Kyiv.
What is behind Seoul's need for secrecy?
There are several reasons why South Korea wanted to keep the POW transfer secret, Erwin Tan, a professor of international politics at Hankuk University, told DW.
"The first was that revealing that the POWs had been repatriated to South Korea would result in Pyongyang retaliating against the families of the men for surrendering," Tan said.
"Seoul also wanted to maintain a channel for communication with Pyongyang," Tan said. "This is a major consideration for the left-leaning wing of Korean politics, which includes President Lee and has historically favored seeking rapprochement with the North."
Kim Sang-woo, a former politician with the left-leaning South Korean Congress for New Politics and now a member of the board of the Kim Dae-jung Peace Foundation, agrees that the South Korean government wanted to avoid "friction" with the North.
But Kim pointed out that it was always very likely that both Moscow and Pyongyang would find out about the transfer sooner or later and that Lee was being criticized in some quarters at home for appearing weak.
"There is criticism that Lee's administration is effectively appeasing the North, that it has become too soft, and that is a very worrisome situation," Kim said. Yet he admits to being surprised at how quickly the issue escalated.
"I think Lee was very angry that he was publicly being accused of lying about the agreement and it rapidly grew into a very messy confrontation," he said.
Has Zelenskyy's approach backfired?
While it is unclear why Zelenskyy used his high-profile UN speech to announce the repatriation of the two POWs, Kim believes it may have been a calculated move to win more support from Seoul.
Kyiv could have carried out a prisoner swap with the Russians and won the freedom of some of its own men in return.
But, Kim pointed out, Ukraine instead chose to accede to Seoul's request in the hope that South Korea would respond with additional financial and possibly even military support. That move appears to have backfired.
Professor Tan anticipates that the two governments will continue to "vent steam" over the issue.
"Given the high profile nature of the mutual accusations, both sides will probably engage in a mutual blame game for the immediate future, but I doubt that it will turn into a long-term case of mutual acrimony," he said.
"I anticipate that after the furor has died down and the press is looking for the next new story, both sides will quietly resume contact on the basis of mutual pragmatism."
Edited by: Karl Sexton
